title.zh: 卷二百五十 列傳第九 石守信 王審琦 高懷德 韓重贇 張令鐸 羅彥瓌 王彥昇
title.en: Volume 250 Biographies 9: Shi Shouxin, Wang Shenqi, Goa Huaide, Han Zhongyun, Zhang Lingduo, Luo Yanggui, Wang Yanshen
title.raw: 卷二百五十 列傳第九 石守信 王審琦 高懷德 韓重贇 張令鐸 羅彥瓌 王彥昇 Volume 250 Biographies 9: Shi Shouxin, Wang Shenqi, Goa Huaide, Han Zhongyun, Zhang Lingduo, Luo Yanggui, Wang Yanshen

sentences.zh: 石守信

translations.literal: Shi Shouxin
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shouxin

sentences.zh: 乾德初，帝因晚朝與守信等飲酒，酒酣，帝曰：「我非爾曹不及此，然吾為天子，殊不若為節度使之樂，吾終夕未嘗安枕而臥。」

translations.literal: Early in Qiande, because of a late court session the Emperor drank wine with Shouxin and the others; when the wine had gone deep, the Emperor said, "If not for you all I would not have reached this; yet as Son of Heaven I am far less happy than when I was a military governor — I have never lain a whole night with my head on a pillow in peace."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiande reign, after a late session at court the emperor shared wine with Shouxin and his companions. When they were well into their cups he said, "Without you I would never have come this far — yet as emperor I am far less content than I was as a military governor. I have not slept through a single night with an easy mind."

sentences.zh: 守信等頓首曰：「今天命已定，誰復敢有異心，陛下何為出此言耶？」

translations.literal: Shouxin and the others kowtowed and said, "Heaven's mandate is now settled — who would again dare harbor a different intent? Why does Your Majesty speak such words?"
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin and the others kowtowed and said, "Heaven's mandate is settled — who would dare harbor disloyal thoughts? Why does Your Majesty speak this way?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人孰不欲富貴，一旦有以黃袍加汝之身，雖欲不為，其可得乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Who does not desire wealth and honor? Once someone has put a yellow robe on your body, even if you wished not to act, how could you refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Who does not want wealth and rank? If one day someone were to drape a yellow robe over your shoulders, even if you wished to refuse, could you?"

sentences.zh: 守信等謝曰：「臣愚不及此，惟陛下哀矜之。」

translations.literal: Shouxin and the others thanked him and said, "We are too dull to have reached this thought — we beg Your Majesty to pity us."
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin and the others thanked him and said, "We are too dull to have seen this — we beg Your Majesty to show us mercy."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人生駒過隙爾，不如多積金、市田宅以遺子孫，歌兒舞女以終天年。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Human life passes like a horse through a crack — better to amass much gold and buy fields and houses to leave to sons and grandsons, and spend your days with singing boys and dancing girls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Life passes like a horse glimpsed through a crack in the wall. Better to pile up gold and buy estates for your heirs, and pass your days with singers and dancers.

sentences.zh: 君臣之間無所猜嫌，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: Between ruler and minister with no mutual suspicion — is that not good?"
translations.idiomatic: With no suspicion between ruler and subject — would that not be best?"

sentences.zh: 守信謝曰：「陛下念及此，所謂生死而肉骨也。」

translations.literal: Shouxin thanked him and said, "That Your Majesty thinks of this — it is what is called making flesh grow on dead bones."
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin thanked him and said, "That Your Majesty has thought of us in this way — it is as though you had raised the dead and clothed their bones with flesh again."

sentences.zh: 明日，皆稱病，乞解兵權，帝從之，皆以散官就第，賞齎甚厚。

translations.literal: The next day they all claimed illness and begged to relinquish military authority; the Emperor consented, and all took honorary posts and retired to their mansions, with very rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they all pleaded illness and asked to surrender their military commands. The emperor agreed; each took an honorary post and retired to his estate, with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 已而，太祖欲使符彥卿管軍，趙普屢諫，以為彥卿名位已盛，不可復委以兵權，太祖不從。

translations.literal: Later Taizu wished to put Fu Yanqing in charge of the army; Zhao Pu repeatedly remonstrated, holding that Yanqing's fame and rank were already great and that military authority could not again be entrusted to him — Taizu would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizu wished to place Fu Yanqing in command of the army. Zhao Pu remonstrated repeatedly, arguing that Yanqing's fame and rank were already too great to be given military authority again. Taizu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 宣已出，普復懷之，太祖迎謂之曰：「豈非符彥卿事耶？」

translations.literal: The edict had already been issued, but Pu again kept it in his bosom; Taizu met him and said, "Is it not about Fu Yanqing?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict had already been issued, but Pu kept it on his person. Taizu met him and said, "Surely this concerns Fu Yanqing?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「非也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "It is not."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "It is not."

sentences.zh: 因奏他事。

translations.literal: He then reported on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported on other business.

sentences.zh: 既罷，乃出彥卿宣進之，太祖曰：「果然，宣何以復在卿所？」

translations.literal: When the audience was over he produced Yanqing's edict and advanced it; Taizu said, "As expected — how is it that the edict is still with you?"
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended he produced Yanqing's edict and presented it. Taizu said, "Just as I thought — how is it that the edict is still in your possession?"

sentences.zh: 普曰：「臣託以處分之語有侏㒧者，復留之。

translations.literal: Pu said, "Your subject found ambiguous wording in the disposition and kept it back.
translations.idiomatic: Pu said, "Your subject found ambiguous wording in the disposition and held the edict back.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下深思利害，勿復悔。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to ponder deeply the advantages and harms, and regret no more."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh the advantages and harms carefully and not regret this again."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「卿苦疑彥卿，何也？

translations.literal: Taizu said, "You stubbornly suspect Yanqing — why?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "You persist in suspecting Yanqing — why?

sentences.zh: 朕待彥卿厚，彥卿豈負朕耶！」

translations.literal: I treat Yanqing generously — how could Yanqing betray me!"
translations.idiomatic: I have treated Yanqing generously — how could he betray me!"

sentences.zh: 普對曰：「陛下何以能負周世宗？」

translations.literal: Pu replied, "How was Your Majesty able to wrong Emperor Shizong of Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu replied, "How was Your Majesty able to wrong Emperor Shizong of Zhou?"

sentences.zh: 太祖默然，事遂中止。

translations.literal: Taizu fell silent, and the matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu fell silent, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年秋，加守信兼侍中。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year of Kaibao, Shouxin was additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year of Kaibao (973), Shouxin was additionally appointed Concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiping Xingguo reign he was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜中書令，行河南尹，充西京留守。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Henan Intendant, and made Western Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Henan Intendant, and Western Capital garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was given the honorary title Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征范陽，督前軍失律，責授崇信軍節度、兼中書令，俄進封衛國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the campaign against Fanyang; supervising the vanguard he violated discipline and was demoted to military governor of Chongxin Army and Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs; soon he was advanced to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined the campaign against Fanyang. As commander of the vanguard he failed in discipline and was demoted to military governor of the Chongxin circuit while retaining the concurrent post of Director of the Department of State Affairs; he was soon advanced to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙鎮陳州，復守中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to garrison Chenzhou and again held the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Chenzhou and again held the directorship of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年五十七，贈尚書令，追封威武郡王，諡武烈。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged fifty-seven; he was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Weiwu Commandery, with posthumous name Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died at fifty-seven. He was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Weiwu, and given the posthumous name Wulie (Fierce in War).

sentences.zh: 守信累任節鎮，專務聚斂，積財鉅萬。

translations.literal: Shouxin repeatedly held military governorships and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth, accumulating riches in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin held several military governorships in succession and devoted himself to amassing wealth, accumulating a fortune of many tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 尤信奉釋氏，在西京建崇德寺，募民輦瓦木，驅迫甚急，而傭直不給，人多苦之。

translations.literal: He especially believed in Buddhism; in the Western Capital he built Chongde Monastery, conscripting the people to haul tiles and timber with very harsh compulsion, yet wages were not paid — many suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to Buddhism. In the Western Capital he built Chongde Monastery, pressing the people to haul tiles and timber with great severity while withholding their wages, and many suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 子保興、保吉。

translations.literal: His sons were Baoxing and Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Baoxing and Baoji.

sentences.zh: 子 保興

translations.literal: Son: Baoxing
translations.idiomatic: Son: Baoxing

sentences.zh: 保興，字光裔，本名保正，太祖取興宗之義改之。

translations.literal: Baoxing, style name Guangyi, original name Baozheng — Taizu changed it, taking the sense of "raising the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing, style name Guangyi, was originally named Baozheng. Taizu renamed him, taking the sense of "glorifying the ancestral line."

sentences.zh: 建隆初，年十四，以蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: Early in Jianlong, aged fourteen, by hereditary privilege he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianlong reign, at fourteen, he entered office by hereditary privilege as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷尚食副使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗召功臣子弟詢以時事，保興年最少，應對明白，太祖奇之，拜如京使。

translations.literal: Taizu once summoned the sons of meritorious ministers to question them on current affairs; Baoxing was youngest in years, yet his replies were clear — Taizu marveled at him and appointed him Commissioner on Mission to the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once summoned the sons of his chief ministers to question them on affairs of state. Baoxing was the youngest, yet his answers were lucid. Taizu was impressed and appointed him Commissioner on Mission to the Capital.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，領順州刺史。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he held the post of prefect of Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao period he served as prefect of Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，為御砦四面都巡檢。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Hedong, he was made Grand Inspector on all four sides of the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Hedong, Baoxing served as Grand Inspector on all four sides of the imperial encampment.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，出為高陽關監軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he went out as military supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he was posted as military supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 守信卒，起復，領本州團練使。

translations.literal: When Shouxin died, he was recalled from mourning and held the post of regimental commissioner of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouxin died he was recalled from mourning to serve as regimental commissioner of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，契丹擾邊，與戴興、楊守一並為澶州前軍駐泊。

translations.literal: Early in Yongxi the Khitans harassed the border; together with Dai Xing and Yang Shouyi he was stationed with the forward army at Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongxi reign, when the Khitans raided the frontier, he was stationed with Dai Xing and Yang Shouyi as part of the forward army garrisoned at Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷入鈔，徙銀、夏、綏府都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian raided in, he was transferred to be Grand Inspector of Yin, Xia, Sui, and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian raided the frontier, Baoxing was transferred to serve as Grand Inspector of Yin, Xia, Sui, and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 嘗巡按罨子砦，並黑水河，趣谷中，夏人知之，以數千騎據險，渡河求戰。

translations.literal: He once inspected Yanzi Fort along the Black Water River and pressed into the valley; the Tangut learned of it and with several thousand horsemen seized the defiles, crossed the river, and sought battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while inspecting Yanzi Fort along the Black Water River, he pressed into a valley. The Tangut learned of it and sent several thousand horsemen to hold the defiles, cross the river, and offer battle.

sentences.zh: 保興所部不滿二千人，乃分短兵伏於河滸，俟其半渡，急擊之，斬首百餘級，追北數十里，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: Baoxing's command numbered fewer than two thousand; he therefore divided short weapons troops to lie in ambush on the river bank, waited until they were half across, then struck urgently — beheading more than a hundred, pursuing north several tens of li; an excellent edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing had fewer than two thousand men. He posted light troops in ambush along the riverbank, waited until the enemy were half across, then attacked fiercely. They took more than a hundred heads and pursued the foe north for several tens of li. An imperial edict singled him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，知平戎軍，徙莫州，俄為西京都巡檢使。

translations.literal: During Duangong he governed Pingrong Army, was transferred to Mozhou, and soon became Western Capital metropolitan inspector.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duangong period he governed Pingrong Army, was transferred to Mozhou, and soon became metropolitan inspector of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，真拜蘄州團練使，為永興軍鈐轄，改夏、綏、麟、府州鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was truly appointed regimental commissioner of Qizhou, made Controller of Yongxing Army, then changed to Controller of Xia, Sui, Lin, and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was formally appointed regimental commissioner of Qizhou, made Controller of the Yongxing army, and later Controller of Xia, Sui, Lin, and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，徙延州都巡檢使兼署州事，改本路副都部署，與范重召等五路討賊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was transferred to Grand Inspector of Yanzhou while concurrently administering prefectural affairs, changed to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of this circuit, and with Fan Zhongzhao and others on five routes campaigned against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was transferred to Grand Inspector of Yanzhou with concurrent charge of prefectural affairs, made Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the circuit, and joined Fan Zhongzhao and others in a five-route campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 有岌伽羅膩數族率眾來拒，保興選敢死士數百人銜枚夜擊，殲之。

translations.literal: The Jiagaluo Ni clans led their masses to resist; Baoxing selected several hundred dare-to-die troops who took sticks in their mouths and struck by night, annihilating them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiagaluo Ni tribes led their forces to resist. Baoxing chose several hundred volunteers, had them take sticks between their teeth, and attacked by night, destroying the enemy.

sentences.zh: 自是吳移、越移諸族歸降。

translations.literal: From this the Wuyi, Yueyi, and other clans submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Wuyi, Yueyi, and other tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 還，至烏、白池，賊又為方陣來拒。

translations.literal: On the return, reaching Black and White Pools, the bandits again formed square arrays to resist.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, at Black and White Pools, the rebels again formed battle lines to block him.

sentences.zh: 保興麾眾出入陣中，會乘馬中流矢，挺身持滿，易騎奮呼，且行且鬥，凡三日四十二戰，賊遂引去。

translations.literal: Baoxing directed his troops in and out of the formations; his horse was struck by a flying arrow — he straightened his body, drew the bow full, changed horses and shouted fiercely, fighting as he went; in all three days and forty-two battles, and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing led his men in and out of the enemy lines. When his horse was struck by an arrow he stood upright, drew his bow to the full, changed mounts, and fought on with fierce cries. Over three days he fought forty-two engagements, and the rebels finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，知威虜軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he governed Weilu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he governed Weilu Army.

sentences.zh: 會夏人入鈔，保興發官帑錢數萬緡分給戰士，主者固執不可。

translations.literal: When the Tangut raided in, Baoxing disbursed several tens of thousands of strings from the official treasury to distribute among the warriors; the custodian stubbornly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided, Baoxing drew several tens of thousands of strings from the official treasury to pay the troops. The treasury officer refused adamantly.

sentences.zh: 保興曰：「城危如此，安暇中覆，事定，覆而不允，願以家財償之。」

translations.literal: Baoxing said, "The city is in such peril — how is there leisure to report to the center? When the affair is settled, if the report is not approved I am willing to repay from family wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing said, "The city is in such peril — there is no time to seek approval from the capital. When this is over, if the court disapproves I will repay the sum from my own estate."

sentences.zh: 夏人退，驛置以聞，真宗貸而不問。

translations.literal: The Tangut withdrew; he reported through the courier stations; Zhenzong pardoned and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut withdrew he reported the matter by courier. Zhenzong pardoned him and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 三年，就拜棣州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed on the spot as defense commissioner of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed defense commissioner of Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 徙知邢州，改澶州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Xingzhou, then changed to Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xingzhou, then to Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡頗峻刑罰，每捶人，令緩施其杖，移晷方畢。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he was quite severe in punishments; whenever he flogged someone he ordered the strokes applied slowly, and only when the sundial had moved a mark was it finished.
translations.idiomatic: In his prefecture he was notably harsh in punishment. When he had someone flogged he ordered the strokes applied slowly, and the beating was not finished until the sundial had moved a full mark.

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾求歸京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on grounds of illness he begged to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he asked to return to the capital on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子元孫。

translations.literal: His son was Yuansun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yuansun.

sentences.zh: 保興世豪貴，累財鉅萬，悉為季弟保從之子所廢。

translations.literal: Baoxing's family for generations were grandees; he amassed wealth in the tens of thousands — all was squandered by the son of his youngest brother Baocong.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing came from a family of great wealth and rank and had amassed a fortune of many tens of thousands, but all of it was squandered by his nephew, the son of his youngest brother Baocong.

sentences.zh: 子 保吉

translations.literal: Son: Baoji
translations.idiomatic: Son: Baoji

sentences.zh: 保吉，字祐之，初以蔭補天平軍衙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: Baoji, style name Youzhi, at first by hereditary privilege was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Inner Yamen of Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji, style name Youzhi, first entered office by hereditary privilege as Commander-in-Chief of the Inner Yamen of the Tianping army.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，召見，賜襲衣、玉帶、金鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he was summoned to audience and granted court robes, jade belt, and horse with golden saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he was summoned to audience and granted court robes, a jade belt, and a horse with golden saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 選尚太祖第二女延慶公主，拜左衛將軍、駙馬都尉，俄領愛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was chosen to marry Taizu's second daughter Princess Yanqing, appointed General of the Left Guard and Commander of the Imperial Sons-in-Law, and soon held the post of prefect of Aizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen to marry Taizu's second daughter, Princess Yanqing, and was appointed General of the Left Guard and Commander of the Imperial Sons-in-Law; he soon served as prefect of Aizhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，遷本州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to defense commissioner of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiping Xingguo reign he was made defense commissioner of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐遣親吏市竹木秦、隴間，矯制度關，為王仁贍所發，罰一季俸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for sending a personal clerk to buy bamboo and timber between Qin and Long, falsely passing customs under forged regulations, exposed by Wang Renzan — fined one season's salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was fined one season's salary after Wang Renzan exposed him for sending a personal clerk to buy bamboo and timber in the Qin-Long region and passing customs under forged papers.

sentences.zh: 七年，改朔州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was changed to surveillance commissioner of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made surveillance commissioner of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 守信卒，起復，為威塞軍節度。

translations.literal: When Shouxin died, he was recalled from mourning and made military governor of Weisai Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouxin died he was recalled from mourning to serve as military governor of the Weisai army.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，出知河陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he went out to govern Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was posted to govern Heyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，召入，復命知大名府兼兵馬都部署，連改橫海、安國二鎮節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned in and again ordered to govern Daming Prefecture while concurrently Commander-in-Chief of troops and horses; he was successively changed to military governor of the two circuits Henghai and Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled and again appointed prefect of Daming with concurrent command of troops and horses; he was then transferred in succession to the Henghai and Anguo circuits.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加檢校太尉、保平軍節度。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was made Honorary Grand Commandant and military governor of Baoping Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Baoji was made Honorary Grand Commandant and military governor of the Baoping army.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，命為河北諸路行營都部署，屯定州。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured north, he was ordered to be Commander-in-Chief of the field headquarters of all Hebei routes, encamped at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north, Baoji was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the field headquarters of all Hebei routes and encamped at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，改武寧軍節度、同平章事。

translations.literal: Early in Jingde he was changed to military governor of Wuning Army and Concurrent Councilor of Equal Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde reign he was made military governor of the Wuning army and Concurrent Councilor of Equal Rank.

sentences.zh: 冬，幸澶淵，命與李繼隆分為駕前東西面都排陣使，軍於北門外。

translations.literal: In winter the emperor visited Chanyuan; he was ordered with Li Jilong to divide as Grand Marshals of Array on the east and west before the imperial carriage, encamping outside the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor went to Chanyuan. Baoji and Li Jilong were appointed Grand Marshals of Array on the east and west before the imperial carriage, with their armies camped outside the north gate.

sentences.zh: 遼騎數萬驟至城下，保吉不介馬而馳當其鋒，遼人引去。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Liao horsemen suddenly reached below the walls; Baoji without donning armor rode to meet their vanguard, and the Liao withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Liao horsemen suddenly appeared below the walls. Baoji rode out without armor to meet their charge, and the Liao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄而請盟，錫宴射于行宮後苑。

translations.literal: Before long they sought alliance; a feast with archery was granted in the rear garden of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Liao sought peace. The emperor granted a feast with archery in the rear garden of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 帝謂繼隆等曰：「自古北邊為患，今其畏威服義，息戰安民，卿等力也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Jilong and the others, "Since antiquity the northern border has been a affliction; now they fear our might and submit to righteousness, warfare ceases and the people are at peace — this is your strength."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Jilong and the others, "The northern frontier has been a scourge since antiquity. Now they fear our might and submit to our rule, and war gives way to peace — this is your doing."

sentences.zh: 保吉進曰：「臣受命禦患，上稟成算。

translations.literal: Baoji advanced and said, "Your subject received the command to repel the affliction and above received the completed plan.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji stepped forward and said, "Your subject received the command to repel the enemy and followed Your Majesty's completed plan.

sentences.zh: 至於布列行陣，指授方略，皆出於繼隆。」

translations.literal: As for deploying battle lines and directing strategy — all came from Jilong."
translations.idiomatic: As for deploying the battle lines and directing strategy, that was all Jilong's work."

sentences.zh: 繼隆曰：「宣力用心，躬率將士，臣不及保吉。」

translations.literal: Jilong said, "In exerting strength with full intent and personally leading generals and soldiers — your subject does not match Baoji."
translations.idiomatic: Jilong said, "In exerting himself wholeheartedly and leading the troops in person, I cannot match Baoji."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿等協和，共致太平，軍旅之事，朕復何憂。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "You harmonize together and jointly bring about great peace — in military affairs, what further worry have I?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You work in harmony and together have brought peace. In military affairs, what have I left to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 歡甚，賜以襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: Very pleased, he granted court robes, gold belt, and saddle and bridle horse.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased, he granted them court robes, gold belts, and horses with saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 二年，改鎮安軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to military governor of Zhen'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to military governor of the Zhen'an army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，自治所來朝，願奉朝請，從之。

translations.literal: Before long, from his own post he came to court, wishing to attend court audiences — this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he came to court from his post and asked to attend regular audiences; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 四年，部民上治狀，乞還鎮所，詔獎諭之，仍從其請。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the people of his district submitted a report on his governance, begging him to return to his garrison — an edict praised and instructed him, and still granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the people of his district submitted a petition praising his governance and asking him to return to his post. An edict commended him and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，從東封，攝司徒，封祀壇奉俎，加檢校太師還鎮。

translations.literal: Early in Dazhong Xiangfu he followed the eastern feng sacrifice, acting as Minister of Education, offering the meat tray at the feng altar, was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu period he accompanied the eastern feng sacrifice as acting Minister of Education, presenting the offering tray at the altar. He was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 冬，公主疾，詔歸視，主薨。

translations.literal: In winter the princess fell ill; an edict ordered him to return to attend her — the princess died.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the princess fell ill. An edict ordered him home to attend her, but she died before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 明年，保吉卒，年五十七，贈中書令，諡莊武。

translations.literal: The next year Baoji died, aged fifty-seven; he was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs, with posthumous name Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Baoji died at fifty-seven. He was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous name Zhuangwu (Solemn in War).

sentences.zh: 保吉姿貌環碩，頗有武幹。

translations.literal: Baoji's bearing was round and large, with considerable martial capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji was large and imposing in bearing and showed considerable martial ability.

sentences.zh: 累世將相，家多財，所在有邸舍、別墅，雖饌品亦飾以彩繢。

translations.literal: For generations generals and ministers, the family had much wealth; wherever he was there were town houses and villas — even food was adorned with colored embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: His family had produced generals and ministers for generations and possessed great wealth. Wherever he went he maintained town houses and villas, and even his meals were served on embroidered vessels.

sentences.zh: 好治生射利，性尤驕倨，所至峻暴好殺，待屬吏不以禮。

translations.literal: He loved managing livelihood and pursuing profit; his nature was especially proud and arrogant — wherever he went he was harsh, violent, and fond of killing, treating subordinate officials without courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to making money and grasping profit. He was especially proud and overbearing, harsh and bloodthirsty wherever he served, and treated his subordinates without courtesy.

sentences.zh: 鎮大名也，葉齊、查道皆知名士，嘗械以運糧。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Daming, Ye Qi and Zha Dao were both renowned scholars — he once had them shackled to transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Daming he once had the renowned scholars Ye Qi and Zha Dao shackled and put to hauling grain.

sentences.zh: 初，程能為京西轉運，保吉託治其私負，能不從。

translations.literal: Earlier Cheng Neng was transport commissioner of Jingxi; Baoji entrusted him to settle his private debts — Neng would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cheng Neng was transport commissioner of Jingxi, Baoji asked him to settle a private debt. Neng refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，其子宿為屬邑吏，將辱之，會有辟召乃止。

translations.literal: At this time his son Su was a clerk in a subordinate county — he was about to humiliate him, but there happened to be a summons for appointment and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Now Neng's son Su served as a clerk in a county under Baoji's jurisdiction. Baoji was about to humiliate him, but stopped when Su received a summons to another post.

sentences.zh: 又染家貸錢，息不盡入，質其女，其父上訴，真宗亟命遣還。

translations.literal: Again he lent money to the Ran family; the interest was not fully paid in — he took the daughter in pawn; her father appealed upward, and Zhenzong urgently ordered her returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also lent money to the Ran family. When they failed to pay the interest in full he took their daughter as security. Her father appealed to the throne, and Zhenzong immediately ordered her released.

sentences.zh: 嘗有僕侵盜私積，不時求對，懇請配隸，帝曰：「是有常法，不可。」

translations.literal: Once a servant stole from his private stores; without waiting for the proper time he sought audience and earnestly begged to have him registered as a bondsman; the Emperor said, "There is regular law for this — it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Once a servant stole from his private stores. Without waiting for the proper audience he begged the emperor to have the man registered as a bondsman. The emperor said, "There is established law for this — it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 保吉請不已，帝戒勖之。

translations.literal: Baoji pleaded without cease; the Emperor admonished and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji kept pleading. The emperor admonished him and urged restraint.

sentences.zh: 善弋獵，畜鷙禽獸數百，令官健羅鳥雀飼之，人有規勸者輒怒之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at archery and hunting, keeping several hundred fierce birds and beasts; he ordered official soldiers to spread nets for sparrows to feed them — whoever admonished him he grew angry at.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at archery and hunting and kept several hundred fierce birds and beasts, ordering his soldiers to net sparrows to feed them. Anyone who remonstrated with him incurred his anger.

sentences.zh: 在陳州，盛飾廨舍以迓貴主。

translations.literal: At Chenzhou he lavishly decorated the official residence to welcome the honored lady.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenzhou he lavishly decorated the official residence to welcome an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 因完葺城壘，疏牖於上，以瞰衢路，如箭窗狀。

translations.literal: He therefore completed repairing the ramparts, opened windows above to overlook the thoroughfare, in the shape of arrow-slits.
translations.idiomatic: He had the ramparts repaired and opened windows along the top to overlook the main road, shaped like arrow-slits.

sentences.zh: 未嘗上聞，賓佐諫之不聽，頗涉眾議。

translations.literal: He never reported it upward; his staff remonstrated but he would not listen — much public talk was involved.
translations.idiomatic: He never reported this to the court. His staff remonstrated with him, but he would not listen, and the matter drew considerable public criticism.

sentences.zh: 初，守信鎮陳，五十七年卒，及保吉繼是鎮，壽亦止是，談者異之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shouxin had garrisoned Chen and died at fifty-seven; when Baoji succeeded to the same garrison, his years of life likewise stopped at this — talkers found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shouxin had governed Chenzhou and died at fifty-seven. When Baoji succeeded to the same post, his life ended at the same age, which observers found remarkable.

sentences.zh: 保吉子貽孫，任崇儀使、帶御器械，坐事免官。

translations.literal: Baoji's son Yisun held the post of Commissioner of Honored Rites and Bearer of Imperial Arms; for an offense he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji's son Yisun served as Commissioner of Honored Rites and Bearer of Imperial Arms but was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 孝孫，西京左藏庫使。

translations.literal: Xiaosun was Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun served as Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 孫 元孫

translations.literal: Grandson: Yuansun
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Yuansun

sentences.zh: 元孫，字善長，始名慶孫，避章獻太后祖諱易之。

translations.literal: Yuansun, style name Shanchang, original name Qingsun — changed to avoid the taboo name of Empress Dowager Zhangxian's ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun, style name Shanchang, was originally named Qingsun. He changed his name to avoid the taboo on the name of Empress Dowager Zhangxian's ancestor.

sentences.zh: 以守信蔭為東頭供奉官、閣門祗候，累遷如京副使。

translations.literal: By Shouxin's hereditary privilege he was made Eastern Head Attendant-in-Ordinary and Ceremonial Attendant at the Gate, and successively promoted to Vice Commissioner on Mission to the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Through Shouxin's hereditary privilege he became Eastern Head Attendant-in-Ordinary and Ceremonial Attendant at the Gate, and was later promoted to Vice Commissioner on Mission to the Capital.

sentences.zh: 康定初，夏人寇延州，元孫與戰于三川口，軍敗見執。

translations.literal: Early in Kangding the Tangut raided Yanzhou; Yuansun fought them at Sankou Pass, the army was defeated and he was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangding reign the Tangut raided Yanzhou. Yuansun fought them at Sankou Pass, his army was defeated, and he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 傳者以為已死，贈忠正軍節度使兼太傅，錄其子孫七人。

translations.literal: Rumor held that he was already dead; he was posthumously made military governor of Zhongzheng Army and Concurrent Grand Tutor, and seven of his sons and grandsons were enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor held that he was dead. He was posthumously made military governor of the Zhongzheng army and Concurrent Grand Tutor, and seven of his sons and grandsons were enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 及元昊納款，縱元孫歸。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao submitted, Yuansun was released to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao submitted to the Song, Yuansun was released and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 諫官御史奏元孫軍敗不死，辱國，請斬塞下。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials and censors memorialized that Yuansun did not die though the army was defeated, disgracing the state — they begged execution at the border.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials and censors memorialized that Yuansun had survived a defeated army and disgraced the state, and asked that he be executed at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 賈昌朝獨言曰：「在春秋時，晉獲楚將穀臣，楚獲晉將知罃，亦還其國不誅。」

translations.literal: Jia Changchao alone spoke: "In Spring and Autumn times, Jin captured the Chu general Guyin, and Chu captured the Jin general Zhi Ying — each also returned him to his state without execution."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Changchao alone argued, "In Spring and Autumn times, when Jin captured the Chu general Guyin and Chu captured the Jin general Zhi Ying, each side returned the captive without execution."

sentences.zh: 因入對，探袖出《魏志于禁傳》以奏曰：「前代將臣，敗覆而還，多不加罪。」

translations.literal: He thereupon entered audience, drew from his sleeve the "Biography of Yu Jin" from the Records of Wei and presented it, saying: "Generals and ministers of former ages who failed and returned were mostly not punished."
translations.idiomatic: He then entered audience, drew from his sleeve the biography of Yu Jin from the Records of Wei, and presented it, saying, "Generals of former ages who were defeated and returned were usually not punished."

sentences.zh: 帝乃貸元孫，安置全州。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Yuansun and settled him at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon pardoned Yuansun and settled him at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以升祔赦，內徙襄州。

translations.literal: Because of the amnesty for the elevation of the ancestral temple, he was moved inward to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under an amnesty issued for the elevation of the imperial ancestral temple, he was moved inland to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉湜言：「元孫失軍辱命，朝廷貸而不誅，若例從量移，無以勸用命之士。」

translations.literal: Censor Liu Yu said: "Yuansun lost the army and disgraced his commission; the court pardoned without execution — if by precedent he is allowed a measured transfer, there is no way to encourage those who devote their lives to duty."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Yu said, "Yuansun lost his army and disgraced his commission. If the court pardons him without execution and then allows a routine transfer, there will be no way to encourage men who stake their lives on duty."

sentences.zh: 元孫遂不徙。

translations.literal: Yuansun was therefore not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun was therefore not transferred.

sentences.zh: 後徙許州，還京師卒。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Xuzhou, returned to the capital and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Xuzhou, returned to the capital, and died there.

sentences.zh: 王審琦

translations.literal: Wang Shenqi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenqi

sentences.zh: 王審琦，字仲寶，其先遼西人，後徙家洛陽。

translations.literal: Wang Shenqi, style name Zhongbao — his ancestors were people of Liaoxi, later the family moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenqi, style name Zhongbao, came from a family originally of Liaoxi that later moved to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，隸周祖帳下，性純謹，甚親任之。

translations.literal: Early in Han Qianyou he served under Zhou Taizu, was pure and careful in nature, and was greatly favored and entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han Qianyou reign he entered the service of Zhou Taizu. Pure and careful by nature, he was greatly favored and trusted.

sentences.zh: 從平李守貞，以功署廳直左番副將。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Li Shouzhen, for merit he was appointed Deputy Commander of the Left Rotation in the Hall Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign that pacified Li Shouzhen and, for his merit, was appointed deputy commander of the left rotation in the Hall Guard.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，歷東西班行首、內殿直都知、鐵騎指揮使，從世宗征劉崇，力戰有功，遷東西班都虞候，改鐵騎都虞候，轉本軍右第二軍都校。

translations.literal: During Guangshun he successively held the posts of head of the Eastern and Western Classes, Director of the Inner Palace Guard, and Commander of the Iron Cavalry; following Shizong's campaign against Liu Chong he fought fiercely with merit, was promoted to Commandant of the Eastern and Western Classes, changed to Commandant of the Iron Cavalry, and transferred to Colonel of the Second Army on the Right of that corps.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun period he served successively as head of the Eastern and Western Classes, director of the Inner Palace Guard, and commander of the Iron Cavalry. He accompanied Shizong against Liu Chong, fought with distinction, and was promoted to commandant of the Eastern and Western Classes, then commandant of the Iron Cavalry, and finally colonel of the second right army of that corps.

sentences.zh: 世宗召禁軍諸校宴射苑中，審琦連中的，世宗嘉之，賞齎有加。

translations.literal: Shizong summoned the commanders of the palace army to feast and shoot in the garden; Shenqi hit the target repeatedly — Shizong praised him and added to his rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong summoned the commanders of the palace army to feast and shoot in the imperial garden. Shenqi hit the target repeatedly, and Shizong praised him with extra rewards.

sentences.zh: 俄領勤州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he held the post of prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，擢為殿前都指揮使、領泰寧軍節度。

translations.literal: Early in Song he was promoted to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front Division and held the military governorship of Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division and military governor of the Taining army.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，為御營前洞屋都部署，為飛石所傷，車駕臨視。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Li Jun, he was made Commander-in-Chief of the forward covered works of the imperial camp, was wounded by a catapult stone, and the imperial carriage came to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Jun he served as commander of the forward covered works of the imperial camp. Wounded by a catapult stone, he was visited by the emperor in person.

sentences.zh: 澤、潞平，改領武成軍節度。

translations.literal: When Ze and Lu were pacified, he was changed to hold the military governorship of Wucheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Ze and Lu were pacified, he was made military governor of the Wucheng army.

sentences.zh: 李重進叛，副石守信為前軍部署討之。

translations.literal: When Li Chongjin rebelled, he served as deputy to Shi Shouxin as forward army commander to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chongjin rebelled, he served under Shi Shouxin as deputy commander of the forward army sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，出為忠正軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he went out as military governor of Zhongzheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he was posted as military governor of the Zhongzheng army.

sentences.zh: 在鎮八年，為政寬簡。

translations.literal: In the garrison eight years, his governance was lenient and simple.
translations.idiomatic: He governed his post for eight years with a lenient and straightforward administration.

sentences.zh: 所部邑令以罪停其錄事吏，幕僚白令不先咨府，請按之。

translations.literal: A county magistrate in his district for an offense suspended his recording clerk; a staff member reported that the magistrate had not first consulted the prefectural office and asked to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: A county magistrate under his jurisdiction suspended a recording clerk for an offense. A staff member reported that the magistrate had acted without first consulting the prefectural office and asked that he be investigated.

sentences.zh: 審琦曰：「五代以來，諸侯強橫，令宰不得專縣事。

translations.literal: Shenqi said: "Since the Five Dynasties, regional lords have been overbearing and magistrates could not exclusively manage county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi said, "Since the Five Dynasties, regional lords have been overbearing and magistrates could not govern their counties independently.

sentences.zh: 今天下治平，我忝守藩維，而部內宰能斥去黠吏，誠可嘉爾，何按之有？」

translations.literal: Now the realm is governed in peace; I am unworthy to guard a frontier, yet a magistrate within my district can drive out a crafty clerk — this is truly praiseworthy — why investigate?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace. Though I am unworthy to guard a frontier post, a magistrate in my district who can drive out a crafty clerk is truly praiseworthy. Why investigate him?"

sentences.zh: 聞者歎服。

translations.literal: Those who heard sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of this sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，從征太原，為御營四面都巡檢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he followed the campaign against Taiyuan as Grand Inspector on all four sides of the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he joined the campaign against Taiyuan as grand inspector on all four sides of the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 三年，改鎮許州，賜甲第，留京師。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to garrison Xuzhou, granted a fine mansion, and remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Xuzhou, granted a fine mansion, and remained at the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗召審琦宴射苑中，連中的，賜御馬、黃金鞍勒。

translations.literal: Taizu once summoned Shenqi to feast and shoot in the garden; he hit the target repeatedly and was granted an imperial horse with golden saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once summoned Shenqi to feast and shoot in the imperial garden. Shenqi hit the target repeatedly and was granted an imperial horse with a golden saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 六年，與高懷德並加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he and Gao Huaide were together made Concurrent Councilors of Equal Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he and Gao Huaide were both made Concurrent Councilors of Equal Rank.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年五十。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died at fifty.

sentences.zh: 初，審琦暴疾，不能語，帝親臨視，及卒，又幸其第，哭之慟。

translations.literal: Earlier Shenqi suffered a sudden illness and could not speak; the Emperor personally came to visit him; when he died the Emperor again visited his mansion and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenqi fell suddenly ill and could not speak, the emperor visited him in person. After his death the emperor again went to his mansion and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 賜中書令，追封琅琊郡王，賻贈加等。

translations.literal: He was granted the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Langya Commandery, with funeral gifts of elevated grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed as Prince of Langya, and granted funeral gifts of the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 葬日，又為廢朝。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, court was again suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his burial the court again suspended audiences.

sentences.zh: 審琦重厚有方略，尤善騎射。

translations.literal: Shenqi was grave, substantial, and resourceful, especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi was grave, substantial, and resourceful, and was especially skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 鎮壽春，歲得租課，量入為出，未嘗有所誅求。

translations.literal: Garrisoning Shouchun, each year he received rent and tax revenues, measured income against expenditure, and never made any exactions.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Shouchun he measured income against expenditure from the annual rents and taxes and never made exactions.

sentences.zh: 素不能飲，嘗侍宴，太祖酒酣仰祝曰：「酒，天之美祿；

translations.literal: He had never been able to drink; once attending a feast, Taizu when deep in wine looked up and prayed: "Wine is Heaven's beautiful bounty;
translations.idiomatic: He had never been able to hold his wine. Once, while attending a feast, Taizu, well into his cups, looked up and prayed, "Wine is Heaven's beautiful bounty;

sentences.zh: 審琦，朕布衣交也。

translations.literal: Shenqi is my friend from commoner days.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi is my friend from the days when I wore plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 方與朕共享富貴，何靳之不令飲邪？」

translations.literal: He is just now sharing wealth and honor with me — why be stingy and not let him drink?"
translations.idiomatic: He is now sharing wealth and honor with me. Why be stingy and not let him drink?"

sentences.zh: 祝畢，顧謂審琦曰：「天必賜卿酒量，試飲之，勿憚也。」

translations.literal: When the prayer was finished he turned to Shenqi and said: "Heaven is sure to grant you capacity for wine — try drinking, do not fear."
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer was finished he turned to Shenqi and said, "Heaven is sure to grant you a capacity for wine. Try drinking, and do not hold back."

sentences.zh: 審琦受詔，飲十杯無苦。

translations.literal: Shenqi received the command and drank ten cups without distress.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi obeyed and drank ten cups without discomfort.

sentences.zh: 自此侍宴常引滿，及歸私家即不能飲，或強飲輒病。

translations.literal: From this, when attending feasts he often drained his cup full, yet returning to his private home he could not drink — if forced to drink he at once fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he often drained his cup at court feasts, but at home he could not drink at all, and if forced to drink would fall ill.

sentences.zh: 子承衍、承衎、承德、承祐、承俊、承偓、承僎、承僅、承休。

translations.literal: His sons were Chengyan, Chengyan, Chengde, Chengyou, Chengjun, Chengwu, Chengzan, Chengjin, and Chengxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chengyan, Chengyan, Chengde, Chengyou, Chengjun, Chengwu, Chengzan, Chengjin, and Chengxiu.

sentences.zh: 承德至西上閣門使、會州刺史；

translations.literal: Chengde rose to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Huizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chengde rose to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Huizhou;

sentences.zh: 承祐至如京使；

translations.literal: Chengyou rose to Commissioner on Mission to the Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou rose to Commissioner on Mission to the Capital;

sentences.zh: 承俊、承僎至內殿崇班；

translations.literal: Chengjun and Chengzan rose to Honored Company of the Inner Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun and Chengzan rose to Honored Company of the Inner Hall;

sentences.zh: 承偓至閣門祗候；

translations.literal: Chengwu rose to Ceremonial Attendant at the Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Chengwu rose to Ceremonial Attendant at the Gate;

sentences.zh: 承僅至左神武將軍致仕；

translations.literal: Chengjin rose to General of the Left Divine Martial Army and retired;
translations.idiomatic: Chengjin rose to General of the Left Divine Martial Army and retired;

sentences.zh: 承休至內殿承制。

translations.literal: Chengxiu rose to Drafter of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu rose to Drafter of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 子 承衍

translations.literal: Son: Chengyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chengyan

sentences.zh: 承衍，字希甫，幼端謹。

translations.literal: Chengyan, style name Xifu, was upright and careful from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyan, style name Xifu, was upright and careful from childhood.

sentences.zh: 審琦鎮袞、滑、壽春，皆署以牙職。

translations.literal: When Shenqi garrisoned Yan, Hua, and Shouchun, he all appointed him to staff posts in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shenqi governed Yan, Hua, and Shouchun, he appointed Chengyan to staff posts at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，補內殿供奉官都知。

translations.literal: Early in Kaibao he was appointed Director of Attendants-in-Ordinary of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaibao period he was appointed Director of Attendants-in-Ordinary of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 三年，尚太祖女昭慶公主，授右衛將軍、駙馬都尉，仍充都知。

translations.literal: In the third year he married Taizu's daughter Princess Zhaoqing, was appointed General of the Right Guard and Commander of the Imperial Sons-in-Law, and still held the directorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he married Taizu's daughter, Princess Zhaoqing, and was appointed General of the Right Guard and Commander of the Imperial Sons-in-Law while retaining his directorship.

sentences.zh: 逾年，領恩州刺史，加本州防禦使。

translations.literal: After a year he held the post of prefect of Enzhou and was made defense commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he served as prefect of Enzhou and was made defense commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，遷應州觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiping Xingguo reign he was made surveillance commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年春，太宗幸其第，賜宴，承衍以金器、名馬為壽，詔賜銀萬兩、錦彩五千匹。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year Taizong visited his mansion and granted a feast; Chengyan presented gold vessels and a famous horse as birthday gifts — an edict granted ten thousand taels of silver and five thousand bolts of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Taizong visited his mansion and granted a feast. Chengyan presented gold vessels and a fine horse as gifts, and an edict granted him ten thousand taels of silver and five thousand bolts of brocade.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Honorary Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Honorary Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 坐市竹木秦、隴，矯制免稅算，罰一季俸。

translations.literal: For buying bamboo and timber in Qin and Long under forged regulations exempting tax calculation, he was fined one season's salary.
translations.idiomatic: He was fined one season's salary for buying bamboo and timber in the Qin-Long region under forged papers exempting him from tax.

sentences.zh: 七年，授彰國軍節度。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was granted the military governorship of Zhangguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made military governor of the Zhangguo army.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，出知天雄軍府兼都部署。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he went out to govern Tianxiong Army headquarters while concurrently Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi period he was posted to govern the Tianxiong headquarters with concurrent command of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 時契丹擾鎮陽，候騎至冀州，去魏二百餘里。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan harassed Zhenyang; scout horsemen reached Jizhou, more than two hundred li from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Khitan were raiding Zhenyang, and their scouts reached Jizhou, little more than two hundred li from Wei.

sentences.zh: 鄰境戒嚴，城中大恐，屬上元節，承衍下令市中及佛寺然燈設樂，與賓佐宴游達旦，人賴以安。

translations.literal: Neighboring districts were on alert and the city was greatly afraid; it happened to be the Lantern Festival — Chengyan ordered lamps lit and music set up in the market and Buddhist temples, feasted and roamed with his staff until dawn, and the people relied on this for reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring districts were on alert and the city was terrified. It happened to be the Lantern Festival. Chengyan ordered lamps lit and music played in the markets and temples, feasted with his staff until dawn, and the people took heart from this display of calm.

sentences.zh: 明年召還，復為貝冀都部署。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned back and again made Commander-in-Chief of Bei and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and again made commander-in-chief of Bei and Ji.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，換永清軍節度，再知天雄軍。

translations.literal: Early in Duangong he was exchanged to military governor of Yongqing Army and again governed Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong period he was transferred to military governor of the Yongqing army and again governed the Tianxiong headquarters.

sentences.zh: 吏民千餘詣監軍，請為本道節帥，詔褒之。

translations.literal: More than a thousand officials and commoners went to the military supervisor, asking that he be made military commissioner of this circuit — an edict praised this.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand officials and commoners petitioned the military supervisor to make him military commissioner of the circuit. An edict commended the request.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改河中尹、護國軍節度，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was changed to Intendant of Hezhong and military governor of Huguo Army, and made Honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Chengyan was made Intendant of Hezhong and military governor of the Huguo army and was given the honorary title Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，以疾求罷節鉞，三抗表不許。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianping, on grounds of illness he begged to relinquish military authority; three memorials of refusal were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianping he asked to resign his military command on grounds of illness, but three memorials were refused.

sentences.zh: 帝自臨問，至臥內慰勉久之，賜予甚厚，擇尚醫數人迭宿其第。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally came to inquire, entered his bedchamber and comforted and encouraged him for a long time, granted very rich gifts, and chose several court physicians to lodge in rotation at his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him in person, entered his bedchamber, and comforted him at length with lavish gifts. Several court physicians were chosen to stay in rotation at his mansion.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨，贈中書令，給鹵簿葬，諡恭肅。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came; he was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs, granted full funeral escort, with posthumous name Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person. Chengyan was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs, granted a full funeral escort, and given the posthumous name Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 其後公主請置守塚五戶，從之。

translations.literal: Afterward the princess asked to establish five households to guard the tomb — this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Later the princess asked that five households be assigned to guard the tomb, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 承衍善騎射，曉音律，頗涉學藝，好吟詠。

translations.literal: Chengyan was skilled at mounted archery, understood music and pitch, was quite versed in learning and arts, and loved composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyan was skilled at mounted archery, understood music, was well versed in the arts of learning, and loved to compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子尚主貴顯，擁富貲，自奉甚厚。

translations.literal: As the son of a meritorious minister who married a princess he was noble and prominent, possessed great wealth, and maintained himself very lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a meritorious minister who had married a princess, he was noble and prominent, possessed great wealth, and lived in considerable luxury.

sentences.zh: 子世安、世隆、世雄、世融。

translations.literal: His sons were Shi'an, Shilong, Shixiong, and Shirong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shi'an, Shilong, Shixiong, and Shirong.

sentences.zh: 世安至崇儀副使、通事舍人。

translations.literal: Shi'an rose to Vice Commissioner of Honored Rites and Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an rose to Vice Commissioner of Honored Rites and Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 世隆，字本支，以公主子為如京副使，歷洛苑、六宅二使、領平州刺史。

translations.literal: Shilong, style name Benzhi, as son of a princess was made Vice Commissioner on Mission to the Capital, successively held the posts of Commissioner of the Luoyang Park and the Six Residences, and held the prefecture of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, style name Benzhi, entered office as son of a princess with the post of Vice Commissioner on Mission to the Capital, later served as commissioner of the Luoyang park and the Six Residences, and held Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 性驕恣，每坐諸叔之上，人皆嗤之。

translations.literal: His nature was proud and willful; he always sat above his various uncles — people all mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: He was proud and willful by nature and always took a seat above his uncles, which people mocked.

sentences.zh: 景德初卒，特贈泰州防禦使。

translations.literal: Early in Jingde he died; he was specially posthumously made defense commissioner of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Jingde reign and was specially posthumously made defense commissioner of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 召見其三子，賜名克基、克緒、克忠，皆面授供奉官。

translations.literal: He summoned and saw his three sons, granted the names Keji, Kexu, and Kezhong, and all were personally appointed Attendants-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned his three sons, granted them the names Keji, Kexu, and Kezhong, and personally appointed each Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 世雄至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Shixiong rose to Honored Company of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong rose to Honored Company of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 世融為內殿承制。

translations.literal: Shirong was Drafter of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong served as Drafter of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 世安子克正殿中丞。

translations.literal: Shi'an's son Kezheng was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an's son Kezheng became Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 克基、克忠並為西染院副使兼閣門通事舍人。

translations.literal: Keji and Kezhong were both Vice Commissioners of the Western Dyeing Bureau and concurrently Masters of Ceremonies at the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Keji and Kezhong both served as vice commissioners of the Western Dyeing Bureau and concurrently as masters of ceremonies at the gate.

sentences.zh: 克緒至內殿承制。

translations.literal: Kexu rose to Drafter of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Kexu rose to Drafter of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 世隆幼子克明為西上閣門副使。

translations.literal: Shilong's youngest son Keming was Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's youngest son Keming became Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 子 承衎

translations.literal: Son: Chengyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chengyan

sentences.zh: 承衎，字希悅，開寶中，授閑廄使，面賜紫袍、金帶，才十二歲。

translations.literal: Chengyan, style name Xiyue — during Kaibao he was appointed Commissioner of the Idle Stables, and in person was granted a purple robe and gold belt at only twelve years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyan, style name Xiyue, was appointed Commissioner of the Idle Stables during the Kaibao period and was personally granted a purple robe and gold belt at only twelve.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，出監徐州軍，又為西京水南巡檢使，改如京使。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he went out to supervise the Xuzhou army, then was made inspector south of the Western Capital waters, and changed to Commissioner on Mission to the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo period he supervised the Xuzhou army, later served as inspector south of the waters of the Western Capital, and was then made Commissioner on Mission to the Capital.

sentences.zh: 表求治郡自效，命知潭州，遷六宅使、領昭州刺史，俄知澶州，加莊宅使。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to govern a prefecture and prove himself; he was ordered to govern Tanzhou, was transferred to Commissioner of the Six Residences and held the prefecture of Shaozhou, soon governed Chunzhou, and was made Commissioner of Imperial Estates.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to govern a prefecture and prove his worth. He was appointed prefect of Tanzhou, later made Commissioner of the Six Residences while holding Shaozhou, soon governed Chunzhou, and was made Commissioner of Imperial Estates.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，兩賜川峽傳詔，慰撫官吏，經略蠻洞。

translations.literal: During Xianping, twice he was granted imperial edicts to the Sichuan gorges, comforting and reassuring officials, and overseeing the Miao cave settlements.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping period he was twice entrusted with imperial edicts to the Sichuan gorges, where he comforted local officials and oversaw the tribal cave settlements.

sentences.zh: 連知延、代、幷三州，皆兼兵馬鈐轄，改尚食使。

translations.literal: In succession he governed Yan, Dai, and Bing — three prefectures — all while concurrently serving as Military Commander-in-Chief, and was changed to Commissioner of Imperial Food.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as prefect of Yan, Dai, and Bing, each time concurrently holding the post of military commander-in-chief, and was then made Commissioner of Imperial Food.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔張雍病，命承衎代之，徙涇州，授下閣門使，改領永州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yong of Fengxiang fell ill, Chengyan was ordered to replace him; he was transferred to Jingzhou, appointed Lower Gate Commissioner, and changed to hold the prefecture of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yong of Fengxiang fell ill, Chengyan was ordered to replace him. He was transferred to Jingzhou, appointed Lower Gate Commissioner, and reassigned to hold Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德中，真宗以天水近邊，蕃漢雜處，擇守臣撫治，擢承衎知秦州，徙知天雄軍。

translations.literal: During Jingde, because Tianshui lay near the frontier where Fan and Han peoples mingled, Zhenzong chose a guardian minister to pacify and govern, promoted Chengyan to govern Qinzhou, and transferred him to govern the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde reign, Zhenzong chose a guardian minister to pacify the border region around Tianshui, where tribal and Han peoples mingled. Chengyan was promoted to prefect of Qinzhou and later transferred to command the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，進秩東上閣門使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, his rank was advanced to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong Xiangfu era he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 承衎病足，在大名不能騎，政多廢馳，及代，賜告家居，表求解職，不允。

translations.literal: Chengyan's feet were afflicted; at Daming he could not ride, and much of his administration was neglected through lack of swift movement. When he was replaced, he was granted leave to remain at home, memorialized asking to resign his post, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyan suffered from a foot ailment. At Daming he could no longer ride, and much of his work went undone because he could not move about quickly. When his term ended he was granted sick leave at home and memorialized asking to resign, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 以久不朝請，求近郡，改左武衛大將軍，知壽州。

translations.literal: Because he had long failed to attend court audiences, he asked for a nearby prefecture, was changed to Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and appointed prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had long been absent from court audiences, he asked for a nearby post and was made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and prefect of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, at age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the era he died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 詔遣其弟承僎馳往護喪。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched his younger brother Chengyin to ride post-haste and oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched his younger brother Chengyin to hurry there and oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 承衎頗涉學，喜為詩，所至為一集。

translations.literal: Chengyan had considerable learning, delighted in composing poetry, and wherever he went compiled a collection.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyan was well read, loved to write poetry, and compiled a collection at each place he served.

sentences.zh: 曉音律，多與士大夫游，意豁如也。

translations.literal: He understood music, associated much with scholar-officials, and his spirit was open and free.
translations.idiomatic: He understood music, kept company with many scholar-officials, and bore himself with an open, easy manner.

sentences.zh: 初，審琦鎮壽春，承衎生於郡廨，至卒亦於其地，人咸異之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shenqi governed Shouchun, Chengyan was born in the prefectural office; when he died it was also in that place — all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shenqi governed Shouchun, Chengyan had been born in the prefectural office; he also died there, and people regarded it as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 子世京為閣門祗候，世文內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His son Shijing was Attendant at the Gate; Shiwen was Honored Company of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shijing served as Attendant at the Gate, and Shiwen as Honored Company of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 孫 克臣 等

translations.literal: Grandson: Ke Chen and others
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Ke Chen, et al.

sentences.zh: 克臣，字子難。

translations.literal: Ke Chen, style name Zinan.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Chen, style name Zinan.

sentences.zh: 祖承衍尚秦國賢穆公主。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chengyin married Princess Xianmu of the State of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chengyin married Princess Xianmu of the State of Qin.

sentences.zh: 克臣第景祐進士，仁宗閱其文，顧侍臣曰：「賢穆有孫登科，可喜也。」

translations.literal: Ke Chen placed in the Jingyou jinshi examinations; Renzong reviewed his essay and, turning to attendant ministers, said, "Princess Xianmu has a grandson who passed the examinations — this is delightful.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Chen passed the jinshi examination in the Jingyou reign. When Renzong reviewed his essay he turned to the attendant ministers and said, "Princess Xianmu has a grandson who has passed the examinations — how delightful.

sentences.zh: 仕累通判壽州。

translations.literal: In office he successively served as vice-prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In office he served in succession as vice-prefect of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 鼓角卒夜入州廨，擊郡將，既就擒，而監兵使所部被甲操刃立庭中，官吏駭觀。

translations.literal: Drum-and-horn soldiers entered the prefectural office at night and struck the prefectural commander; once they had been seized, the supervising military officer had his subordinates arm themselves with blades and stand in the courtyard, while officials looked on in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At night, garrison drum-and-horn troops broke into the prefectural office and attacked the prefectural commander. After they were captured, the supervising military officer had his men don armor, take up blades, and stand in the courtyard while the officials watched in alarm.

sentences.zh: 克臣徐言曰：「此不過為盜耳。」

translations.literal: Ke Chen said calmly, "This is nothing more than banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Chen said calmly, "This is nothing more than robbery.

sentences.zh: 立遣甲者去，戒兇卒勿妄引他人，眾讙服，是日天貺節，率掾屬朝謁如常儀，人賴以安，猶坐貶監潭州稅。

translations.literal: He immediately sent the armored men away, warned the violent soldiers not to implicate others without cause, and the crowd applauded in submission. That day was the Festival of Heaven's Gift; he led his staff in the usual court audience, and the people relied on him and were reassured — yet he was still demoted to supervisor of the Tanzhou tax office.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately dismissed the armored men, warned the ringleaders not to implicate others without cause, and won the crowd's assent. That day was the Festival of Heaven's Gift; he led his staff through the usual court audience, and the people were reassured — yet he was still demoted to supervisor of the Tanzhou tax office.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，為開封、度支二判官，遷鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: During the Xining period he was vice-director of both Kaifeng and the Department of Revenue, then was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining period he served as vice-director of both Kaifeng and the Department of Revenue, then was promoted to vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 時鄭俠以上書竄嶺表，克臣嘗薦俠，且饋之白金，又坐奪官。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Xia was exiled to the southern frontier for submitting a memorial; Ke Chen had once recommended Xia and even presented him with white gold, and for this again lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Xia had been exiled to the southern frontier for submitting a memorial. Ke Chen had once recommended him and even gave him white gold, and for this he again lost his office.

sentences.zh: 復為戶部副使，以集賢殿修撰知鄆州。

translations.literal: He was restored as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and as Academician of the Hall for Treasuring the Classics governed Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and, as Academician of the Hall for Treasuring the Classics, was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 京東多盜，克臣請以便宜處決，遂下諸郡使械送尤桀者斬以徇，盜為少衰。

translations.literal: Bandits were numerous in eastern capital circuit; Ke Chen requested discretionary authority to execute them, and an order was sent to the prefectures to send the most brutal offenders in fetters to be beheaded as a warning — banditry somewhat declined.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rampant in the eastern capital circuit. Ke Chen requested discretionary authority to execute offenders, and an order went out to the prefectures to send the worst offenders in fetters to be beheaded as a warning. Banditry declined somewhat.

sentences.zh: 河決曹村，克臣亟築堤城下，或曰：「河決澶淵，去鄆為遠，且州徙于高，八十年不知有水患，安事此。」

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke at Caocun, Ke Chen urgently built dikes below the city wall. Some said, "The river broke at Chanyuan — Yan is far from there, and the prefecture was moved to higher ground; for eighty years it has known no flood — why bother with this?
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke through at Caocun, Ke Chen urgently built dikes below the city wall. Some said, "The breach was at Chanyuan — Yan is far from there, and the prefectural seat was moved to higher ground; for eighty years it has known no flood. Why bother with this?

sentences.zh: 克臣不聽，役愈急，堤成，水大至，不沒者才尺餘。

translations.literal: Ke Chen would not listen; the corvée labor grew ever more urgent. When the dike was finished, the flood came in force, and only a little over a foot remained above water.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Chen would not listen, and the labor grew ever more urgent. When the dike was finished the flood surged in, and only a little over a foot of the city remained above water.

sentences.zh: 復起甬道，屬之東平王陵埽，人得趨以避水。

translations.literal: He then raised a causeway and connected it to the Wangling embankment at Dongping, so people could hurry along it to escape the water.
translations.idiomatic: He then built a causeway linking it to the Wangling embankment at Dongping, giving people a route to escape the flood.

sentences.zh: 事寧，皆繪像祀之。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, all painted his portrait and worshipped him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed, the people painted his portrait and worshipped him.

sentences.zh: 進天章閣侍制，徙知瀛州，有告外間入境，密旨趣具獄，株連甚眾，克臣陰緩之，已而得為間者於他道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, transferred to govern Yingzhou. When someone reported that an outsider had entered the border, a secret edict urged that the case be completed; many were implicated. Ke Chen secretly slowed the proceedings, and later the spy was caught on another route.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns and transferred to Yingzhou. When someone reported an infiltrator crossing the border, a secret edict pressed for a swift conviction and many were implicated. Ke Chen quietly slowed the case, and the spy was later caught on another route.

sentences.zh: 徙知太原，王中正西討罔功，而誣克臣姑息士卒，使無固志，黜為單州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Taiyuan. Wang Zhongzheng's western campaign achieved nothing, yet he falsely accused Ke Chen of indulging the soldiers and leaving them without firm resolve, and Ke Chen was dismissed to Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiyuan. Wang Zhongzheng's western campaign achieved nothing, yet he falsely accused Ke Chen of coddling the troops and sapping their fighting spirit, and Ke Chen was demoted to Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 至是，神宗幸尚書省，至部舍止輦，獎其治力，以為雖少者不及。

translations.literal: By then Shenzong was visiting the Ministry of Works; when he reached the ministry building he stopped the imperial carriage and praised Ke Chen's administrative strength, saying that even younger men could not match it.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shenzong visited the Ministry of Works. When he reached the ministry building he stopped his carriage and praised Ke Chen's administrative ability, saying that even younger officials could not match him.

sentences.zh: 顧其子駙馬都尉師約使入覲。

translations.literal: He looked to his son, the Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Shi Yue, and ordered him to attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: He then had his son, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Shi Yue, presented at court.

sentences.zh: 元祐四年，以龍圖閣直學士、太中大夫卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyou, as Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and Grand Master of Palace Attendance he died, at age seventy-six.
