translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanyou he died at the age of seventy-six, holding the posts of direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and grand master of palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 師約，字君授，少習進士業。

translations.literal: Shi Yue, style name Junshou, in youth studied for the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue, style name Junshou, studied for the jinshi examinations in his youth.

sentences.zh: 英宗欲求儒生為主婿，命宰相召克臣諭旨，令師約持所為文至第。

translations.literal: Yingzong wished to find a Confucian scholar as imperial son-in-law; he ordered the chief ministers to summon Ke Chen and convey the intent, directing Shi Yue to bring his writings to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong wished to choose a Confucian scholar as imperial son-in-law. He ordered the chief ministers to summon Ke Chen, convey the intent, and have Shi Yue bring his writings to the palace.

sentences.zh: 明日，獻賦一編，即坐中賦《大人繼明詩》，遂賜對，選為駙馬都尉，尚徐國公主。

translations.literal: The next day he presented a collection of fu; on the spot he composed the poem "The Great Man Who Succeeds the Bright," was granted an audience, was selected as Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and married Princess Xu of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he presented a collection of fu and, on the spot, composed the poem "The Great Man Who Succeeds the Bright." He was granted an audience, chosen as imperial son-in-law commandant, and married Princess Xu of the State of Xu.

sentences.zh: 授左衛將軍，面賜玉帶，又賜九經、筆硯，勉之進學。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Guard, was in person granted a jade belt, and was again granted the Nine Classics, brush and inkstone, with encouragement to advance in learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general of the Left Guard, personally granted a jade belt, and given the Nine Classics along with brush and inkstone, with encouragement to continue his studies.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，遷鎮安軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Zhezong acceded, he was transferred to Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Zhen'an Army, remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong acceded he was made military governor and observation commissioner of Zhen'an Army, remaining in office.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后臨朝，師約屢上書言事。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanren held court, Shi Yue repeatedly submitted memorials on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Dowager Xuanren held court, Shi Yue repeatedly submitted memorials on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 元符初，議者以為職不當上言，褫其秩。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanfu, critics held that his office ought not to speak on such matters, and his rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanfu reign critics argued that his office should not address such matters, and his rank was stripped from him.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，乃復保平軍留後，又為樞密都承旨，未幾復罷。

translations.literal: When Huizong acceded, he was restored as regent of Baoping Army, then made Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon was dismissed again.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong acceded he was restored as regent of Baoping Army, then made chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but was soon dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 崇甯元年，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning he died, at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning he died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 師約善射，嘗陪遼使燕射玉津園，一發中鵠，發必破的，屢受金帶及鞍勒馬之賜。

translations.literal: Shi Yue was skilled at archery. Once, while accompanying Liao envoys at an archery feast in Yujin Garden, with one shot he hit the center of the target; every shot struck true, and he repeatedly received gifts of gold belts, saddles, bridles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue was a skilled archer. Once, while entertaining Liao envoys at an archery feast in Yujin Garden, he hit the bullseye with his first shot. Every arrow found its mark, and he received repeated gifts of gold belts, saddles, bridles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 子殊，主所生，至閬州觀察使。

translations.literal: His son Shu, born to the princess, rose to Observation Commissioner of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu, born to the princess, rose to observation commissioner of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 高懷德

translations.literal: Gao Huaide
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huaide

sentences.zh: 高懷德，字藏用，真定常山人，周天平節度齊王行周之子。

translations.literal: Gao Huaide, style name Cangyong, was a native of Changshan in Zhending, and son of Xingzhou, Prince of Qi and Military Governor of the Tianping Circuit of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huaide, style name Cangyong, was a native of Changshan in Zhending and the son of Xingzhou, Prince of Qi and military governor of the Tianping circuit under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 懷德忠厚倜儻，有武勇。

translations.literal: Huaide was loyal, generous, and bold, with martial courage.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide was loyal, generous, and bold, and possessed martial courage.

sentences.zh: 行周歷延、潞二鎮及留守洛都，節制宋、亳，皆署以牙職。

translations.literal: When Xingzhou successively governed Yan and Lu, remained to guard the Luoyang capital, and controlled Song and Bo, he always appointed Huaide to staff positions in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzhou governed Yan and Lu in succession, remained to guard the Luoyang capital, and controlled Song and Bo, he always appointed Huaide to staff positions at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 晉開運初，遼人侵邊，以行周為北面前軍都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun in Jin, when the Khitan invaded the frontier, Xingzhou was made Overall Commander of the Northern Front Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyun era under Jin, when the Khitan invaded the frontier, Xingzhou was made overall commander of the northern front army.

sentences.zh: 懷德始冠，白行周願從北征。

translations.literal: Huaide had just reached adulthood; he told Xingzhou he wished to follow the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide had just come of age and told Xingzhou he wished to join the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 行周壯之，許其行，至戚城遇遼軍，被圍數重，援兵不至，危甚。

translations.literal: Xingzhou admired his spirit and permitted him to go. At Qicheng they encountered Khitan forces, were surrounded many times over, reinforcements did not arrive, and the peril was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou admired his spirit and let him go. At Qicheng they met Khitan forces, were surrounded many times over while reinforcements failed to arrive, and the danger was extreme.

sentences.zh: 懷德左右射，縱橫馳突，眾皆披靡，挾父而出。

translations.literal: Huaide shot left and right, charged and broke through at will; all scattered before him, and he seized his father and broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide shot in every direction, charging and breaking through at will. The enemy scattered before him, and he fought his way out with his father.

sentences.zh: 以功領羅州刺史，賜珍裘、寶帶、名馬以寵異之。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed prefect of Luozhou and was granted a rare fur robe, a precious belt, and a famous horse to honor him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed prefect of Luozhou and was granted a rare fur robe, a precious belt, and a famous horse in special recognition.

sentences.zh: 及行周移鎮鄆州，改信州刺史，仍領牙校。

translations.literal: When Xingzhou was transferred to govern Yanzhou, Huaide was changed to prefect of Xinzhou while still holding his headquarters staff post.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzhou was transferred to govern Yanzhou, Huaide was made prefect of Xinzhou while retaining his headquarters staff post.

sentences.zh: 又遷信州刺史，從行周再鎮宋州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to prefect of Xinzhou and followed Xingzhou when he again governed Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made prefect of Xinzhou and followed Xingzhou when the latter again governed Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉末，契丹南侵，以行周為邢趙路都部署禦之，留懷德守睢陽。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, when the Khitan invaded southward, Xingzhou was made Overall Commander of the Xing-Zhao Route to repel them, and Huaide was left to guard Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin dynasty, when the Khitan invaded southward, Xingzhou was made overall commander of the Xing-Zhao route to repel them, and Huaide was left to guard Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 會杜重威降契丹，京東諸州群盜大起，懷德堅壁清野，敵不能入。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan, bandits rose in great numbers throughout the eastern capital circuit; Huaide strengthened his walls, cleared the countryside, and the enemy could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan, bandits rose throughout the eastern capital circuit. Huaide strengthened his defenses and cleared the countryside, and the enemy could not break in.

sentences.zh: 行周率兵歸鎮，敵遂解去。

translations.literal: Xingzhou led troops back to his command; the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzhou led his troops back to his command, the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 漢初，行周移鎮魏博，及再領天平，以懷德為忠州刺史領職如故。

translations.literal: Early in Han, Xingzhou was transferred to govern Weibo, and when he again held Tianping, Huaide was made prefect of Zhongzhou while holding his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty Xingzhou was transferred to Weibo, and when he again held Tianping, Huaide was made prefect of Zhongzhou while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 周祖征慕容彥超，還過汶上，寵賜行周甚厚，並賜懷德衣帶、彩繒、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned against Murong Yanchao and returned past Wenshang, he richly rewarded Xingzhou and also granted Huaide robes, belts, colored silks, saddles, bridles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder campaigned against Murong Yanchao and returned through Wenshang, he richly rewarded Xingzhou and also granted Huaide robes, belts, colored silks, saddles, bridles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 行周卒，召懷德為東西班都指揮使、領吉州刺史，改鐵騎都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Xingzhou died, Huaide was summoned as Commander of the Eastern and Western Classes and held the prefecture of Ji, then was changed to Commander of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzhou died, Huaide was summoned to serve as commander of the eastern and western classes while holding Jizhou, and was then made commander of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太原劉崇入寇，世宗討之，以懷德為先鋒都虞候。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong of Taiyuan invaded, Shizong campaigned against him and made Huaide Vanguard Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong of Taiyuan invaded, Shizong marched against him and made Huaide vanguard vice commander.

sentences.zh: 高平克捷，以功遷鐵騎右廂都指揮使、領果州團練使。

translations.literal: Victory was won at Gaoping; for his merit he was transferred to Commander of the Right Wing of the Iron Cavalry and held the regimental commissioner post of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Gaoping he was promoted to commander of the right wing of the Iron Cavalry and regimental commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，知廬州行府事，充招安使。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Huainan, managed affairs of the Luzhou field headquarters, and served as Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Huainan, managed affairs at the Luzhou field headquarters, and served as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戰廬州城下，斬首七百餘級。

translations.literal: In battle below Luzhou city he beheaded more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In battle below the walls of Luzhou he took more than seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 尋遷龍捷左廂都指揮使、領岳州防禦使，賜駿馬七匹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commander of the Left Wing of the Dragon Swift and held the defense commissioner post of Yuezhou; he was granted seven fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of the left wing of the Dragon Swift and defense commissioner of Yuezhou, and was granted seven fine horses.

sentences.zh: 南唐將劉仁贍據壽春，舒元據紫金山，置連珠砦為援，以抗周師。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang generals Liu Renzan held Shouchun and Shu Yuan held Purple Gold Mountain; they set up linked-pearl fortifications as support to resist the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang generals Liu Renzan held Shouchun and Shu Yuan held Purple Gold Mountain, building linked-pearl fortifications as support against the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 世宗命懷德率帳下親信數十騎覘其營壘。

translations.literal: Shizong ordered Huaide to lead several dozen trusted horsemen from his personal guard to reconnoiter their encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong ordered Huaide to lead several dozen trusted horsemen from his personal guard to reconnoiter the enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 懷德夜涉淮，遲明，賊始覺來戰，懷德以少擊眾，擒其裨將以還，盡偵知其形勢強弱，以白世宗。

translations.literal: Huaide crossed the Huai by night; at dawn the bandits only then realized and came to fight. Huaide with the few struck the many, captured their vice general and returned, and fully reconnoitered their positions' strength and weakness, reporting all to Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide crossed the Huai by night. At dawn the enemy only then noticed and came to fight. With a small force he struck a large one, captured an enemy vice general, and returned after fully reconnoitering their strength and weakness, reporting everything to Shizong.

sentences.zh: 世宗大喜，賜襲衣、金帶、器幣、銀鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: Shizong was greatly pleased and granted him a ceremonial robe, a gold belt, vessels and silks, and a silver saddle, bridle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was greatly pleased and granted him a ceremonial robe, a gold belt, vessels and silks, and a silver saddle, bridle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 世宗一日因按轡淮壖以觀賊勢，見一將追擊賊眾，奪槊以還，令左右問之，乃懷德也。

translations.literal: One day Shizong, holding the reins on the Huai bank to observe the bandits' strength, saw a general pursue the bandit host, seize a spear, and return. He ordered those beside him to ask who it was — it was Huaide.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as Shizong held the reins on the Huai bank to observe the enemy, he saw a general pursue the enemy host, seize a spear, and ride back. He had those beside him ask who it was — it was Huaide.

sentences.zh: 召至行在慰勞，許以節鋮。

translations.literal: He summoned him to the field headquarters to comfort and reward him, and promised him a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned him to headquarters to comfort and reward him, and promised him a military commission.

sentences.zh: 世宗北征，命與韓通率兵先抵滄州。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned north, he ordered Huaide and Han Tong to lead troops first to reach Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong marched north he ordered Huaide and Han Tong to lead troops to Cangzhou ahead of the main force.

sentences.zh: 初得關南，又命副陳思讓為雄州兵馬都部署，克瓦橋關，降姚內斌以歸。

translations.literal: When the southern passes were first taken, he was again ordered to serve as deputy to Chen Siliang as Overall Military Commander of Xiongzhou, captured Waqiao Pass, and returned after accepting the surrender of Yao Neibin.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern passes were first taken, he was again ordered to serve under Chen Siliang as overall military commander of Xiongzhou, captured Waqiao Pass, and returned after Yao Neibin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，擢為侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領江寧軍節度，又為北面行營馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Huaide was promoted to Commander of the Palace Horse Army and held the military governorship of Jiangning, and again served as Commander of the Northern Campaign Horse Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Huaide was promoted to commander of the palace horse army and military governor of Jiangning, and also served as commander of the northern campaign horse army.

sentences.zh: 懷德將家子，練習戎事，不喜讀書，性簡率，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Huaide was the son of a general's house, practiced in military affairs, did not delight in reading books, and by nature was plain and direct, not bound by small proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide came from a general's household, was trained in military affairs, did not care for books, and was by nature plain and direct, unconcerned with minor proprieties.

sentences.zh: 善音律，自為新聲，度曲極精妙。

translations.literal: He was skilled at music, composed new melodies himself, and set tunes with extreme refinement.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at music, composed new melodies himself, and set tunes with exceptional refinement.

sentences.zh: 好射獵，嘗三五日露宿野次，獲狐兔累數百，或對客不揖而起，由別門引數十騎從禽於郊。

translations.literal: He loved hunting; once he would camp in the open for three or five days and capture foxes and hares by the hundreds. Sometimes before guests he would rise without bowing, leave by another gate, and lead several dozen horsemen to hunt game in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hunting and would sometimes camp in the open for three or five days at a time, taking foxes and hares by the hundreds. Sometimes he would rise before guests without bowing, slip out another gate, and lead several dozen horsemen to hunt in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 子處恭，歷莊宅使至右監門衛大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: His son Chugong rose from Commissioner of Imperial Estates to Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and retired.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chugong rose from commissioner of imperial estates to grand general of the Right Gate Guard, then retired.

sentences.zh: 處俊至西京作坊使。

translations.literal: Chujun rose to Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun rose to commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 韓重贇

translations.literal: Han Chongyun
translations.idiomatic: Han Chongyun

sentences.zh: 韓重贇，磁州武安人。

translations.literal: Han Chongyun was a native of Wu'an in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chongyun was a native of Wu'an in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 少以武勇隸周太祖麾下。

translations.literal: In youth, for martial courage he entered service under the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered service under the Zhou founder for his martial courage.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補左班殿直副都知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed Deputy Chief of the Left Class Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun reign he was appointed deputy chief of the left class palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從世宗戰高平，以功遷鐵騎指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in battle at Gaoping and, for his merit, was transferred to Commander of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong at the battle of Gaoping and, for his merit, was promoted to commander of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，先登中流矢，轉都虞候。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Huainan, was first to ascend and was struck by an arrow in the fighting, and was transferred to Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Huainan, was first to scale the walls and was struck by an arrow in the fighting, and was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 俄遷控鶴軍都指揮使、領虔州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commander of the Crane-Control Army and held the prefecture of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of the Crane-Control Army and prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，以翊戴功，擬為龍捷左廂都校、領永州防禦使。

translations.literal: Early in Song, for merit in supporting the enthronement he was proposed as Colonel of the Left Wing of the Dragon Swift and defense commissioner of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty, for merit in supporting the enthronement he was proposed as colonel of the left wing of the Dragon Swift and defense commissioner of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 從征澤、潞還，命代張光翰為侍衛馬步軍都指揮使、領江寧軍節度。

translations.literal: Returning from the campaign against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to replace Zhang Guanghan as Commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Armies and military governor of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the campaign against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to replace Zhang Guanghan as commander of the palace horse and foot armies and military governor of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 討李重進，為行營馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Li Chongjin he served as Vice Commander of the Field Headquarters Horse and Foot Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Chongjin he served as vice commander of the field headquarters horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，改殿前都指揮使、領義成軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was changed to Commander of the Palace Front Army and military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he was made commander of the palace front army and military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，發京畿丁壯數千，築皇城東北隅，且令有司繪洛陽宮殿，按圖修之，命重贇董其役。

translations.literal: In the third year he mobilized several thousand strong men from the capital region to build the northeastern corner of the imperial city, and also ordered the relevant offices to paint the Luoyang palace halls and repair them according to the plans; Chongyun was ordered to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he mobilized several thousand strong men from the capital region to build the northeastern corner of the imperial city. He also ordered the relevant offices to paint the Luoyang palace halls and repair them according to the plans, placing Chongyun in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年秋，河決澶州，命重贇督丁壯數十萬塞之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Qiande, the Yellow River broke at Chunzhou; Chongyun was ordered to supervise several hundred thousand strong men in blocking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year of Qiande the Yellow River broke at Chunzhou, and Chongyun was ordered to supervise several hundred thousand laborers in blocking the breach.

sentences.zh: 四年，太祖郊祀，以為儀仗都部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Taizu performed the suburban sacrifice, Chongyun was made Overall Commander of the Ceremonial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Taizu performed the suburban sacrifice, Chongyun was made overall commander of the ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 時有譖贇私取親兵為腹心者，太祖怒，欲誅之。

translations.literal: At the time someone slandered Chongyun, saying he privately took personal guards as his inner circle; Taizu was angry and wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone slandered Chongyun, claiming he had taken personal guards as his private inner circle. Taizu was enraged and wished to execute him.

sentences.zh: 趙普諫曰：「親兵，陛下必不自將，須擇人付之。

translations.literal: Zhao Pu remonstrated and said, "The personal guard — Your Majesty surely will not command them yourself; you must choose someone to entrust them to.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu remonstrated and said, "The personal guard — Your Majesty surely will not command them yourself; you must choose someone to entrust them to.

sentences.zh: 若重贇以讒誅，即人人懼罪，誰復為陛下將親兵者？。」

translations.literal: If Chongyun is executed on slander, then everyone will fear guilt — who again will command the personal guard for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: If Chongyun is executed on false charges, then everyone will fear punishment — who again will command the personal guard for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 太祖納其言，重贇得不誅。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his counsel, and Chongyun was spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu accepted his advice, and Chongyun was not put to death.

sentences.zh: 後聞普嘗救己，即詣普謝，普拒不見。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that Pu had once saved him, he went to Pu to thank him; Pu refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When he later learned that Zhao Pu had once saved his life, he went to thank him, but Pu refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，出為彰德軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, he was dispatched as military governor of the Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year he was posted out as military governor of the Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖征太原，過其郡，重贇迎謁于王橋頓，召赴燕飲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan; passing through his commandery, Chongyun welcomed and paid respects at Wangqiao Station and was summoned to a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao, when Taizu marched on Taiyuan and passed through his jurisdiction, Chongyun came out to greet him at Wangqiao Station and was invited to a banquet.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「契丹知我是行，必率眾來援，彼意鎮、定無備，必由此路入。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The Khitans know of this campaign and will surely lead troops to assist; they will think Zhen and Ding are unprepared and will certainly enter by this route.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Khitans know I am on this expedition and will surely bring troops to relieve the city. They will assume Zhen and Ding are undefended and will certainly come in by this road.

sentences.zh: 卿為我領兵倍道兼行，出其不意，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: You shall lead troops for me at forced march day and night; catch them unprepared and you will surely defeat them."
translations.idiomatic: Lead my troops at forced march and take them by surprise — you are certain to break them."

sentences.zh: 乃命為北面都部署。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Overall Northern Commander.
translations.idiomatic: With that he was made overall commander of the northern front.

sentences.zh: 重贇令軍士銜枚夜發，果遇契丹兵於定州，見重贇旗幟，大駭欲引去，重贇乘之，大破其眾，獲馬數百匹。

translations.literal: Chongyun ordered the soldiers to take wood in their mouths and set out at night; they indeed encountered Khitan troops at Dingzhou; seeing Chongyun's banners they were greatly terrified and wished to withdraw; Chongyun pressed the advantage and routed their forces, capturing several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyun had his men march at night with gag-sticks in their mouths. At Dingzhou they ran into Khitan forces who, seeing Chongyun's banners, were so alarmed they tried to pull back. Chongyun pressed the attack, smashed their army, and took several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased and issued an edict of special praise.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and sent down a gracious edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died and was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 重贇信奉釋氏，在安陽六七年，課民采木為寺，郡內苦之。

translations.literal: Chongyun believed in Buddhism; during six or seven years at Anyang he levied the people to gather timber for temples, and the commandery suffered grievously.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyun was a devout Buddhist. During the six or seven years he spent at Anyang he pressed the people to cut timber for temples, and the whole commandery groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 子崇訓、崇業。

translations.literal: His sons were Chongxun and Chongye.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chongxun and Chongye.

sentences.zh: 重贇與張光翰、趙彥徽分領諸軍節度，嘉其翊戴功也。

translations.literal: Chongyun, together with Zhang Guanghan and Zhao Yanhui, were assigned to hold various military governorships — in recognition of their meritorious support at the enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyun, Zhang Guanghan, and Zhao Yanhui were given separate military governorships in reward for their service in supporting the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 光翰，後唐山南節度使虔劍兄子，及卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Guanghan was the nephew of Qian Jian, Military Governor of Shannan under Later Tang; upon his death he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan was a nephew of Qian Jian, military governor of Shannan under Later Tang. When he died he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 彥徽，真定安喜人，與太祖同事世宗，太祖兄事之，及卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Yanhui was a native of Anxi in Zhending; he had served Shizong together with Taizu, and Taizu treated him as an elder brother; upon his death he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was from Anxi in Zhending. He had served alongside Taizu under Shizong, and Taizu treated him as an elder brother. When he died he too was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子 崇訓

translations.literal: Son: Chongxun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chongxun

sentences.zh: 崇訓，字知禮，乾德中，以蔭補供奉官，遷西京作坊副使，出為澶州河南北都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Chongxun, courtesy name Zhili; during Qiande, through yin privilege he was made Attendant Official; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Western Capital Workshops; he was dispatched as Metropolitan North-South Patrol Commissioner of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun, courtesy name Zhili, entered service through yin privilege in the Qiande era as an attendant official. He was promoted to vice director of the Western Capital workshops, then sent out as metropolitan north-south patrol commissioner of Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 從太宗征河東，還，以貝、冀等州都巡檢使權知麟州。

translations.literal: Accompanying Taizong on the Hedong campaign, upon return he was made Metropolitan Patrol Commissioner of Bei, Ji, and other prefectures, with acting authority over Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong on the Hedong campaign and, on returning, was made metropolitan patrol commissioner for Bei, Ji, and other prefectures with acting charge of Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，李繼遷寇夏州，崇訓領兵赴援，大敗之。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, Li Jiqian raided Xia Prefecture; Chongxun led troops to assist and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, when Li Jiqian attacked Xia Prefecture, Chongxun marched to its relief and routed him.

sentences.zh: 徙監夏州軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to oversee the Xia Prefecture garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to supervise the garrison at Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷知越、泉、登、莫四州，徙知威虜軍，改如京使。

translations.literal: He successively governed the four prefectures of Yue, Quan, Deng, and Mo; he was transferred to govern Weilu Army; he was changed to Envoy Bearing Credentials for the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Yue, Quan, Deng, and Mo, then was moved to govern Weilu Army and promoted to envoy bearing credentials for the capital.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，出知石州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was dispatched to govern Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianping era he was posted out to govern Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬繼遷犯境，崇訓追襲之，至賀蘭山而還。

translations.literal: When Jiqian violated the frontier, Chongxun pursued and attacked him, returning after reaching Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian raided the border, Chongxun pursued him as far as Helan Mountain before turning back.

sentences.zh: 二年，再知麟州，又敗繼遷於城下。

translations.literal: In the second year he again governed Lin Prefecture and again defeated Jiqian below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was again put in charge of Lin Prefecture and once more defeated Jiqian beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 崇訓由河西徙閩、越，再移北邊，凡二十五年，以勞擢西上閣門使、邠甯環慶清遠軍都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Chongxun moved from the Hexi region to Min and Yue, then again to the northern frontier — altogether twenty-five years; for his labors he was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Metropolitan Patrol Commissioner of Bin-Ning, Huanqing, and Qingyuan Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun served first in the Hexi corridor, then in Min and Yue, and then on the northern frontier for twenty-five years in all. For his long service he was promoted to western upper gate commissioner and metropolitan patrol commissioner of the Bin-Ning, Huanqing, and Qingyuan armies.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮、定、高陽關行營鈐轄，屯鎮州，兼河北都轉運使事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Camp Controller of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass Field Headquarters, stationed at Zhen Prefecture, concurrently handling affairs as Metropolitan Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as camp controller for the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass field headquarters, stationed at Zhen Prefecture, and also handled the duties of metropolitan transport commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 契丹兵至方順河，將寇威虜軍，崇訓陳兵唐河，扼其要路。

translations.literal: Khitans troops reached Fangshun River and were about to raid Weilu Army; Chongxun deployed troops at Tang River, blocking their vital route.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan forces reached the Fangshun River and were poised to strike Weilu Army, Chongxun drew up his men on the Tang River and blocked the key crossing.

sentences.zh: 敵遣別騎寇赤堠驛崇，崇訓分兵擒戮之。

translations.literal: The enemy sent separate cavalry to raid Chichao Station; Chongxun divided his forces and captured and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent a detached cavalry column against Chichao Station; Chongxun divided his force, captured the raiders, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 既而值霖雨，敵兵饑乏不敢進，遂遁去。

translations.literal: Before long continual rain set in; the enemy troops were hungry and short of supplies and dared not advance, and so fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon heavy rains set in. The enemy, hungry and short of supplies, dared not press forward and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 移幷、代鈐轄，權知幷州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Controller of Bing and Dai, with acting authority over Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to controller of Bing and Dai with acting charge of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從部署張進領兵由土門會大將王超，襲破契丹於定州。

translations.literal: Following Deployer Zhang Jin, he led troops through Tumen Pass to join the great general Wang Chao and launched a surprise attack that routed the Khitans at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under deployer Zhang Jin he led troops through Tumen Pass to join the commander Wang Chao and struck the Khitans at Dingzhou, breaking them completely.

sentences.zh: 六年，授四方館使、樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was granted the posts of Commissioner of the Four Directions Hostel and Chief Liaison of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made commissioner of the Four Directions Hostel and chief liaison of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 又命為鎮、定、高馬步軍都鈐轄，屯定州。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to serve as Overall Controller of Zhen, Ding, and Gao infantry and cavalry, stationed at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed overall controller of the Zhen, Ding, and Gao infantry and cavalry forces, with his headquarters at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，契丹入寇至唐河，崇訓陳兵河南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde the Khitans invaded and reached Tang River; Chongxun deployed troops south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingde era the Khitans invaded as far as the Tang River, and Chongxun drew up his army on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又與王超追襲至鎮州。

translations.literal: The next day he again joined Wang Chao in pursuit as far as Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he joined Wang Chao in pursuit all the way to Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而都部署桑贊逗留不進，崇訓帥兵獨往。

translations.literal: Before long the Overall Deployer Sang Zan lingered without advancing; Chongxun led his troops forward alone.
translations.idiomatic: When overall deployer Sang Zan hung back and would not advance, Chongxun marched forward on his own.

sentences.zh: 時車駕幸澶州，召崇訓，乃還。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was at Chunzhou; Chongxun was summoned and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Chunzhou; Chongxun was recalled and returned.

sentences.zh: 三年春，拜檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was appointed Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was made honorary grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，授右龍武軍大將軍，領韶州防禦使，以本官分司西京卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was made General of the Right Dragon Martial Army and Defender of Shaozhou; he died while serving in his original rank at the Western Capital nominal post, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was appointed general of the Right Dragon Martial Army and defender of Shaozhou. He died while holding his existing rank in a nominal post at the Western Capital, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 崇訓為人長厚謙畏，未嘗忤物。

translations.literal: Chongxun was by nature generous, modest, and cautious; he never gave offense to others.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was open-hearted, modest, and careful; he never gave offense to anyone.

sentences.zh: 子允恭，禮賓副使，有謀略，好學，人以為能世其家云。

translations.literal: His son Yungong was Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception; he was resourceful and fond of learning; people thought him capable of carrying on the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yungong served as vice commissioner of ceremonial reception. Clever and studious, he was regarded as able to uphold the family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 子 崇業

translations.literal: Son: Chongye
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chongye

sentences.zh: 崇業，字繼源，以蔭補供奉官，選尚秦廷美女雲陽公主，授左臨門衛將軍、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Chongye, courtesy name Jiyuan; through yin privilege he was made Attendant Official; selected to marry the beautiful Princess Yunyang of the Qin court, he was granted General of the Left Linmen Guard and Commissioner as Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Chongye, courtesy name Jiyuan, entered service through yin privilege as an attendant official. Chosen to marry the celebrated Princess Yunyang of the Qin court, he was made general of the Left Linmen Guard and commissioner as imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 廷美得罪，降為右千牛衛率府率，分司西京，俄削秩，去駙馬之號，從貶房陵。

translations.literal: When Tingmei fell from grace, he was demoted to Colonel of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard Commandery, given a nominal post at the Western Capital; soon his rank was stripped and the title of imperial son-in-law removed; he was exiled with Tingmei to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingmei was disgraced, Chongye was reduced to colonel of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard commandery with a nominal post at the Western Capital. Soon his rank was stripped, his title as imperial son-in-law was removed, and he was banished with Tingmei to Fangling.

sentences.zh: 廷美卒，起為靜難軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Tingmei died, he was recalled as Acting Military Affairs Secretary of Jingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Tingmei died he was recalled and made acting military affairs secretary of the Jingnan Army.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，授甯州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was made Prefect of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 公主卒，葬州境。

translations.literal: When the princess died, she was buried within the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess died she was buried within his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，始得入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign he was at last permitted to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the beginning of Zhenzong's reign was he allowed to come to court again.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，改左屯衛大將軍、領高州團練使，追封公主為虢國長公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he was changed to General of the Left Tunwei Guard and Regimented Trainer of Gaozhou; the princess was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping he was made general of the Left Tunwei Guard and regimented trainer of Gaozhou, and the princess was posthumously enfeoffed as grand princess of the state of Guo.

sentences.zh: 五年十月，卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, aged forty-one.

sentences.zh: 子允升為內殿承制、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Yunsheng became Inner Hall Artisan and Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yunsheng rose to inner hall artisan and gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 張令鐸

translations.literal: Zhang Lingduo
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingduo

sentences.zh: 令鐸本名鐸，以與河中張鐸同姓名，故賜今名。

translations.literal: Lingduo's original given name was Duo; because someone named Zhang Duo in Hezhong shared the same name, he was granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Lingduo was originally named Duo. Because a Zhang Duo in Hezhong bore the same name, the court granted him his present name.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷馬步軍都虞候、領陳州節制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to Chief Adjutant of Horse and Foot Armies and charged with control of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was promoted to chief adjutant of the horse and foot armies with charge of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖征李筠，以令鐸為東京舊城內都巡檢。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Li Jun, Lingduo was made Metropolitan Inner Patrol Commissioner of the Old City of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched against Li Jun, Lingduo was made metropolitan inner patrol commissioner of the old city of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，出為鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was dispatched as military governor of Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he was posted out as military governor of the Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 帝為皇弟興元尹光美娶其第三女。

translations.literal: The Emperor had his younger brother, Prince of Xingyuan Yin Guangmei, marry Lingduo's third daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had his younger brother, Prince of Xingyuan Yin Guangmei, marry Lingduo's third daughter.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，來朝被病，車駕臨問，賜帛五千匹、銀五千兩，並賜其家人甚厚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he came to court afflicted by illness; the imperial carriage came in person to inquire after him; he was granted five thousand bolts of silk and five thousand taels of silver, and his family were also granted very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he came to court ill. The emperor visited him in person, bestowed five thousand bolts of silk and five thousand taels of silver, and gave his family lavish gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 明年春，卒于京師，年六十。

translations.literal: The following spring he died in the capital, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he died in the capital, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悲悼，贈侍中。

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved deeply and posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 令鐸性仁恕，嘗語人曰：「我從軍三十年，大小四十餘戰，多摧堅陷敵，未嘗妄殺一人。」

translations.literal: Lingduo was by nature humane and forgiving; he once told others, "I have served in the army for thirty years, in more than forty battles large and small; I have often smashed strong positions and routed the enemy, yet I have never killed a person without cause."
translations.idiomatic: Lingduo was humane and forgiving by nature. He once told others, "I have been in the army for thirty years and fought more than forty battles, large and small. I have often broken strong positions and routed the enemy, yet I have never killed anyone without cause."

sentences.zh: 及卒，人多惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, many mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, many grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 子守正，至內園使。

translations.literal: His son Shouzheng rose to Inner Garden Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouzheng rose to inner garden commissioner.

sentences.zh: 守恩，淳化中，累至崇儀副使，稍遷崇儀使，領錦州刺史，。

translations.literal: Shou'en — during Chunhua he rose successively to Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies, then was gradually promoted to Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies and charged as Prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en, during the Chunhua era, rose step by step to vice commissioner of honored ceremonies, then was promoted to commissioner of honored ceremonies with charge of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景德初，知原州，就加西上閣門使、知泰州，卒，。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he governed Yuan Prefecture; he was then additionally made Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Governor of Taizhou; he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingde era he governed Yuan Prefecture, was then additionally made western upper gate commissioner and prefect of Taizhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 錄其子奉禮郎永安為大理評事，後至殿中丞。

translations.literal: His son Yong'an, Gentleman for Ceremonial Reception, was enrolled as Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review; he later rose to Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong'an, a gentleman for ceremonial reception, was enrolled as a case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and later rose to palace secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 羅彥瓌

translations.literal: Luo Yanggui
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yanggui

sentences.zh: 羅彥瓌，幷州太原人。

translations.literal: Luo Yanggui was a native of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yanggui was a native of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父全德，晉泌州刺史，彥瓌得補內殿直。

translations.literal: His father Quande was Prefect of Bi Prefecture under Jin; Yanggui obtained appointment as Inner Hall Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quande had been prefect of Bi under Jin. Yanggui entered service as an inner hall attendant.

sentences.zh: 少帝在澶州，欲命使宣慰大名府，時河北契丹騎充斥，遂募軍中驍勇士十人從行，彥瓌備選。

translations.literal: When the Lesser Emperor was at Chunzhou he wished to dispatch an envoy to console Daming Prefecture; at the time Khitan cavalry filled Hebei; ten fierce brave men from the army were recruited to accompany the mission; Yanggui was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: While the Lesser Emperor was at Chunzhou he wanted to send an envoy to reassure Daming Prefecture. Khitan horsemen covered Hebei, so ten of the army's bravest men were chosen to escort the mission; Yanggui was one of them.

sentences.zh: 銜枚夜發，往返如期，由是補興順指揮使。

translations.literal: They took wood in their mouths and set out at night; the round trip was completed on schedule; for this he was appointed Commander of Xingshun.
translations.idiomatic: They marched at night with gag-sticks in their mouths and returned on time. For this Yanggui was appointed commander of the Xingshun unit.

sentences.zh: 開運末，契丹主至汴，遣彥瓌送廄馬千匹赴幽薊，彥瓌至元氏，聞漢祖建號太原，以馬歸漢，漢祖嘉之。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitan ruler reached Bian; he dispatched Yanggui to deliver a thousand stable horses to Youji; Yanggui reached Yuanshi, heard that Han Zu had established his title at Taiyuan, and brought the horses over to Han; Han Zu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitan ruler reached Bian and sent Yanggui to deliver a thousand remounts to Youji. At Yuanshi Yanggui learned that Han Zu had proclaimed himself at Taiyuan, turned the horses over to him, and was commended.

sentences.zh: 及入汴，擢為護聖指揮使。

translations.literal: When he entered Bian he was promoted to Commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Han entered Bian, Yanggui was promoted to commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 周初，遷散員都虞候，坐樞密使王浚黨，出為鄧州教練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was transferred to Chief Adjutant of the Loose Ranks; implicated as a partisan of Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun, he was dispatched as Training Commissioner of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhou dynasty he became chief adjutant of the loose ranks, but as a partisan of the bureau commissioner Wang Jun he was sent out as training commissioner of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，召為伴飲指揮使，改馬步軍都軍頭。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne he was recalled as Commander of the Companion Guard and changed to Chief General of Horse and Foot Armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne he was recalled as commander of the Companion Guard and made chief general of the horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 從向訓收秦、鳳有功，遷散指揮都虞候。

translations.literal: Following Xiang Xun he captured Qin and Feng with merit and was transferred to Chief Adjutant of the Loose Command.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xiang Xun in the capture of Qin and Feng, distinguished himself, and was made chief adjutant of the loose command.

sentences.zh: 顯德末，太祖自陳橋入歸公署，見宰相范質等，未及言，彥瓌不挺劍而前曰：「我輩無主，今日須天子。」

translations.literal: At the end of Xiande, Taizu returned from Chenqiao to the public office and saw the Chancellor Fan Zhi and others; before he could speak, Yanggui stepped forward without drawing his sword and said, "We have no master — today we must have an emperor."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xiande, when Taizu came back from Chenqiao Bridge to the government offices and met the chancellor Fan Zhi and the others, Yanggui stepped forward before he could speak and declared, "We have no ruler — today there must be an emperor."

sentences.zh: 質等由是降階聽命。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi and the others thereupon descended the steps and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: At that Fan Zhi and the others came down the steps and submitted.

sentences.zh: 擢為控鶴左廂都指揮使，改內外馬軍都軍頭、領眉州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander of the Left Wing of the Crane Control Guard, changed to Chief General of Inner and Outer Horse Armies, and charged as Defender of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the left wing of the Crane Control Guard, made chief general of the inner and outer horse armies, and given charge of Meizhou as defender.

sentences.zh: 從平澤、潞還，命代趙彥徽為侍衛步軍都指揮使、領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: Returning from pacifying Ze and Lu, he was ordered to replace Zhao Yanhui as Commander of the Palace Foot Guard and charged as military governor of Wuxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Ze and Lu he was ordered to replace Zhao Yanhui as commander of the palace foot guard and military governor of the Wuxin Army.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，出為彰德軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was dispatched as military governor of Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he was posted out as military governor of the Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，改安國軍節度，與昭義軍節度李繼勳大破契丹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he was changed to military governor of Anguo Army; together with Li Jixun, military governor of Zhaoyi Army, he inflicted a great defeat on the Khitans.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he was transferred to the Anguo Army and, together with Li Jixun of the Zhaoyi Army, won a great victory over the Khitans.

sentences.zh: 四年春，又與閣門使田欽祚殺太原軍千餘人于靜陽，禽其將鹿英等，獲馬三百匹。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, together with Gate Commissioner Tian Qinzuo, he killed more than a thousand Taiyuan troops at Jingyang, captured their generals Lu Ying and others, and seized three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he and gate commissioner Tian Qinzuo killed more than a thousand Taiyuan troops at Jingyang, captured generals such as Lu Ying, and took three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 明年，移鎮華州。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to govern Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he died, aged forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 王彥昇

translations.literal: Wang Yanshen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanshen

sentences.zh: 王彥昇，字光烈，性殘忍多力，善擊劍，號「王劍兒」。

translations.literal: Wang Yanshen, courtesy name Guanglie; cruel by nature and possessed of great strength; skilled at swordplay; known as "Sword Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanshen, courtesy name Guanglie, was cruel, immensely strong, and skilled with the sword. Men called him "Sword Wang."

sentences.zh: 本蜀人，後唐同光中，蜀平，徙家洛陽。

translations.literal: Originally a man of Shu; during Tongguang of Later Tang, when Shu was pacified, his family moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally from Shu. When Shu was conquered in the Tongguang era of Later Tang, his family moved to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初事宦官驃騎大將軍孟漢瓊，漢瓊以其趫勇，言于明宗，補東班承旨。

translations.literal: At first he served the eunuch General of Fast Cavalry Meng Hanqiong; Hanqiong, owing to his swift bravery, spoke of him to Mingzong, and he was appointed Eastern Class Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the eunuch general of fast cavalry Meng Hanqiong. Impressed by his swift courage, Hanqiong recommended him to Mingzong, and he was made an eastern-class attendant.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，轉內殿直。

translations.literal: During Tianfu of Jin he was transferred to Inner Hall Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Jin he was transferred to inner hall attendant.

sentences.zh: 開運初，契丹圍大名，少帝幸澶州，募勇敢士齎詔納城中，彥昇與羅彥瓌應之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun the Khitans besieged Daming; the Lesser Emperor went to Chunzhou; brave men were recruited to carry an edict into the city; Yanshen and Luo Yanggui responded.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyun, when the Khitans besieged Daming and the Lesser Emperor withdrew to Chunzhou, brave men were sought to carry an imperial message into the city. Yanshen and Luo Yanggui answered the call.

sentences.zh: 一夕突圍而入，以功遷護聖指揮使。

translations.literal: In one night they broke through the encirclement and entered; for this merit he was transferred to Commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In a single night they broke through the lines and entered the city. For this feat Yanshen was made commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，從向拱破太原兵虒亭南，斬敵帥王璋於陣，以功遷龍捷右第九軍都虞候。

translations.literal: During Guangshun of Zhou, following Xiang Gong he defeated Taiyuan troops south of Si Ting and slew the enemy commander Wang Zhang in battle; for this merit he was transferred to Chief Adjutant of the Right Ninth Army of Dragon Swift.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun of Zhou he followed Xiang Gong in defeating Taiyuan forces south of Si Ting and killed the enemy commander Wang Zhang in the field. He was then made chief adjutant of the right ninth army of Dragon Swift.

sentences.zh: 累轉鐵騎右第二軍都校、領合州刺史。

translations.literal: He was successively transferred to Commandant of the Right Second Army of Iron Cavalry and charged as Prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to commandant of the right second army of Iron Cavalry and was given charge of He Prefecture as prefect.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮南，從劉崇進、宗偓破金牛水砦，禽偽軍校閻承旺、范橫。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned against Huainan, following Liu Chongjin and Zong Wo he captured the Jinniu River fort and took the false-regime officers Yan Chengwang and Fan Heng.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's Huainan campaign he followed Liu Chongjin and Zong Wo in taking the Jinniu River fort and captured the enemy officers Yan Chengwang and Fan Heng.

sentences.zh: 又從李重進扞吳兵于盛唐，斬二千人餘級。

translations.literal: Again following Li Chongjin he blocked Wu troops at Sheng Tang and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Li Chongjin in holding off Wu forces at Sheng Tang and killed more than two thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又從張永德攻瀛州，下束城，改散員都指揮使。

translations.literal: Again following Zhang Yongde he attacked Ying Prefecture, took Shucheng, and was changed to Commander of the Loose Ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Zhang Yongde in the attack on Ying Prefecture, captured Shucheng, and was made commander of the loose ranks.

sentences.zh: 太祖北征，至陳橋，為眾推戴。

translations.literal: On Taizu's northern expedition, at Chenqiao Bridge he was acclaimed by the troops.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizu's northern expedition, at Chenqiao Bridge the army acclaimed him as emperor.

sentences.zh: 彥昇以所部先入京，遇韓通于路，逐至第殺之。

translations.literal: Yanshen led his unit into the capital first; encountering Han Tong on the road, he pursued him to his residence and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen led his command into the capital first. He met Han Tong on the road, chased him home, and killed him there.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖誓軍入京不得有秋毫犯，及聞通死，意甚不樂。

translations.literal: At first Taizu had sworn that the army entering the capital must not commit the slightest offense; when he heard of Tong's death he was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had sworn that the troops entering the capital would not harm so much as a blade of grass. When he learned that Tong was dead, he was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 以建國之始，不及罪彥昇，拜恩州團練使、領鐵騎左廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: Because it was the beginning of founding the state, he was not punished in time; he was appointed regimental commissioner of Enzhou and held the post of Commander of the Left Wing of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was not punished in time. Instead he was appointed regimental commissioner of Enzhou and commander of the left wing of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後為京城巡檢，中夜詣王溥第，溥驚悸而出，既坐，乃曰：「此夕巡警甚困，聊就公一醉耳。」

translations.literal: Later he was metropolitan patrol inspector; in the middle of the night he went to Wang Pu's residence — Pu came out startled and fearful; once seated he said, "Tonight's patrol is very tiring — I have come to share a cup with you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Later, as metropolitan patrol inspector, he called on Wang Pu's residence in the middle of the night. Pu came out startled. Once seated, Yanshen said, "Patrol duty tonight has worn me out — I have come only to share a cup with you, sir."

sentences.zh: 彥昇意在求賄，溥佯不悟，置酒數行而罷。

translations.literal: Yanshen's intent was to seek a bribe; Pu pretended not to understand, set out wine for several rounds, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen was seeking a bribe. Pu pretended not to understand, poured a few rounds of wine, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 翌日，溥密奏其事，乃出為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: The next day Pu secretly memorialized the affair, and Yanshen was sent out as prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Pu memorialized the matter in secret, and Yanshen was posted out as prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，遷申州團練使。

translations.literal: Early in Qiande he was transferred to regimental commissioner of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiande reign he was transferred to regimental commissioner of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，改防州防禦使，是冬，又移原州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was changed to defense commissioner of Fangzhou; that winter he was again transferred to Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he was made defense commissioner of Fangzhou. That winter he was transferred again to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 西人有犯漢法者，彥昇不加刑，召僚屬飲宴，引所犯以手捽斷其耳，大嚼，卮酒下之。

translations.literal: When westerners violated Han law, Yanshen did not impose legal punishment; he summoned his staff to drink and feast, brought the offender forward, tore off his ear with his hand, chewed it greatly, and washed it down with a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: When westerners broke Han law, Yanshen would not apply regular punishment. He would summon his staff to feast, bring the offender forward, tear off his ear with his bare hand, chew it, and wash it down with wine.

sentences.zh: 其人流血被體，股慄不敢動。

translations.literal: The man was covered in blood, trembling in his thighs and not daring to move.
translations.idiomatic: The victim would be drenched in blood, trembling and unable to stir.

sentences.zh: 前後㗖者數百人。

translations.literal: Those he bit and chewed before and after numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He did this to several hundred men in all.

sentences.zh: 西人畏之，不敢犯塞。

translations.literal: The westerners feared him and did not dare violate the border passes.
translations.idiomatic: The westerners feared him and did not dare raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 七年，以病代還，次乾州卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on grounds of illness he was replaced and returned; he died while stopped at Qianzhou, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was relieved on grounds of illness and started home. He died at Qianzhou on the way, at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其奪殺韓通，終身不授節鋮。

translations.literal: Taizu, because he had killed Han Tong by force, never granted him military authority for his whole life.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had killed Han Tong, Taizu never granted him military authority for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 論曰：石守信而下，皆顯德舊臣，太祖開懷信任，獲其忠力。

translations.literal: The discussion says: From Shi Shouxin downward, all were old ministers of Xiande; Taizu opened his heart and trusted them, obtaining their loyal strength.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: From Shi Shouxin downward, these were all veterans of the Xiande reign. Taizu trusted them openly and won their loyal service.

sentences.zh: 一日以黃袍之喻，使自解其兵柄，以保其富貴，以遺其子孫。

translations.literal: On one day, by the parable of the yellow robe, he made them release military authority themselves, to preserve their wealth and honor and leave it to sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: On a single occasion, with the parable of the yellow robe, he induced them to surrender military authority themselves, preserving their wealth and rank for themselves and their heirs.

sentences.zh: 漢光武之于功臣，豈過是哉！

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han toward his meritorious ministers — could he surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Guangwu of Han in his treatment of meritorious ministers scarcely surpassed this!

sentences.zh: 然守信之貨殖鉅萬，懷德之馳逐敗度，豈非亦因以自晦者邪？

translations.literal: Yet Shouxin's amassing wealth in the tens of thousands, and Huaide's racing and hunting beyond measure — were these not also ways to obscure themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shouxin's amassing of a vast fortune and Huaide's reckless hunting and racing — were these not also ways to make themselves inconspicuous?

sentences.zh: 至於審琦之政成下蔡，重贇之功宣廣陵，卓乎可稱。

translations.literal: As for Shenqi's governance succeeding at Xia Cai, and Chongyun's achievements proclaimed at Guangling — outstanding and praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi's successful governance at Shouchun and Chongyun's achievements at Guangling stand out as truly praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 令鐸身四十餘戰，未嘗妄殺，可謂勇者之仁矣。

translations.literal: Lingduo personally fought more than forty battles and never killed recklessly — this may be called the humanity of the brave.
translations.idiomatic: Lingduo fought in more than forty engagements and never killed recklessly — this may be called the humanity of a brave man.

sentences.zh: 彥瓌於革命之日，首挺劍以語范質，于宋則未必功在眾先，于周則其過不在人後矣。

translations.literal: Yangui on the day of revolution was first to draw his sword and speak to Fan Zhi — for Song his merit was not necessarily ahead of the multitude, but for Zhou his fault was not behind others.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the revolution Yangui was the first to draw his sword and address Fan Zhi. For the Song his merit was not necessarily foremost, but for the Zhou his fault was certainly not the least.

sentences.zh: 王彥昇殺韓通，太祖雖不加罪，而終身不授節鋮，是足垂訓後人矣。

translations.literal: Wang Yanshen killed Han Tong; although Taizu did not punish him, he never granted military authority for his whole life — this is sufficient to hand down instruction to later men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanshen killed Han Tong. Though Taizu did not punish him, he never granted him military authority for life — enough to instruct posterity.

sentences.zh: 保吉、承衍咸以帝婿致位藩鎮，其被驅策、著戎功，則保吉為優，況推功李繼隆，尤為不伐而有讓，然械役名士，縱意禽荒，累德多矣。

translations.literal: Baoji and Chengyan both reached military governorships as imperial sons-in-law; in being driven to service and achieving military merit, Baoji was superior — moreover, in pushing merit to Li Jilong, he was especially free of boasting and possessed yielding virtue; yet shackling and enslaving renowned scholars and indulging hunting to excess — his accumulated virtue suffered much loss.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji and Chengyan both rose to military governorships as imperial sons-in-law. In active service and military achievement Baoji was the better man, and in crediting Li Jilong he showed a rare unwillingness to boast. Yet he shackled eminent scholars for labor and indulged hunting without restraint, and in these ways he forfeited much of his merit.
